### FD-19 the boundary declaration is a frame per block or a type per definition, and this tree took the second route and is three annotations short of it

- state:    OPEN
- claim:    The question, for `.planning/TAL-CONFORMANCE-QUEUE.md` slice R5: what must a block boundary carry for a target-level checker to be complete, and what obligation does that put on the pass that emits the code? **Two published disciplines put the boundary state into the artifact, and they bill the producer differently by two orders of magnitude.** Route one declares a frame per block: the JVM's `StackMapTable` gives the verification type of every local and every operand stack entry at the start of each basic block, TAL's register-file type is the same object, and WebAssembly's block type is the same object over a nesting tree. Route two types every value where it is defined and declares no frame: LLVM's `phi` carries one type field for the join, and Cranelift's block parameters are typed with every branch obliged to supply arguments that match. Route one moves the dataflow fixpoint from the checker into the producer and its annotation runs to about half the size of the code it annotates. Route two charges the producer only the writing down of what the emitter already computed. **The tree is on route two at every boundary it has, and its one full frame is already written.** `TFn`'s `params` is a positional register-file type over registers `0..n-1` and `seed-params` reads it back. A `tt-case` branch's `dsts` are declared through the scrutinee's `DCtor` field types in `CEnv`, which is the declaration Cranelift and WebAssembly ask for at a boundary. The JVM's frame is a wider object, and the tree has no jump target that would want one. `outline` spells the whole enclosing scope into a `TalSig` for the outlined `name$k`, so FD-15's stack-free alternative to CPS already carries a JVM-shaped frame at its boundary, written as a function signature. **The residue is three annotations and nothing else.** `i-bnew`, `i-bget` and `i-blen` bind a `dst` and carry no `ty`, which is PRB-75, and route two's closure is that every value's type is in the artifact. **The producer that would owe them is `compile-fn`, and it owes nothing today**, because no pass in the typed SSA path originates a byte-cell instruction. **The register allocator has no position, because there is no register allocator**: `nregs` is a frame-slot count and the x64 prologue turns it into one stack slot per SSA register.
- measured: **1. Route one, and the frame is the whole state at the boundary.** JVMS4:12247 "The intent is that a stack map frame must appear at" the beginning of each basic block, specifying the verification type of every operand stack entry and of JVMS4:12250 "each local variable at the start of each basic block. The type checker" reads them and generates a proof from them. Even the first frame is a declaration read off the artifact rather than a walk result, JVMS4:5336 "computed from the method descriptor by the" type checker. Three clauses make the declaration load-bearing. A branch is checked against a declared frame and the checker never computes a target's state: JVMS4:13873 "targetIsTypeSafe(Environment, StackFrame, Target) :-" over JVMS4:13874 "    offsetStackFrame(Environment, Target, Frame),". Where a frame is present the walk state is discarded in its favour: JVMS4:13804 "the type state must be assignable to the one in the" stack map frame, by JVMS4:13811 "    frameIsAssignable(frame(Locals, OperandStack, Flags), MapFrame)," and the tail then runs under `MapFrame`. **That clause is the completeness mechanism**, because a refusal inside one block cannot poison the next block's entry when the entry is read. And the checker refuses to walk code it has no declared state for: JVMS4:13850 "It is illegal to have code after an" unconditional branch without a stack map frame, implemented as JVMS4:13856 "write_ln('No stack frame after unconditional branch')," followed by `fail`. **2. The producer's bill for route one, measured twice.** Leroy states the split and its origin: LEROYBCV:2941 "Inspired by Necula and Lee's proof-carrying code [36], Rose and Rose [47] propose to split bytecode" LEROYBCV:2942 "verification into two phases: the code producer computes the stack and register types at branch" LEROYBCV:2943 "targets and transmit these so-called certificates along with the bytecode; the embedded system," then checks them LEROYBCV:2945 "rather than inferring these types itself. In other terms, the embedded system no longer solves" the dataflow equations iteratively. The gain is the fixpoint, LEROYBCV:2950 "one, since we avoid the cost of the fixpoint iteration. This speeds up verification to some extent". The price is size, and it is the only published figure found for a boundary annotation: LEROYBCV:2956 "A practical limitation of this approach is that certificates are relatively large: about 50% of the" LEROYBCV:2957 "size of the code they annotate [31]. Even if certificates are stored in persistent memory, they can" exceed the available space. **The implementation side says the producer runs the checker's old algorithm.** JDKSTACKMAP:52 " * StackMapGenerator is responsible for stack map frames generation." detects JDKSTACKMAP:59 " *      <li>Mandatory stack map frame include all jump and switch instructions targets," and all handlers, then iterates: JDKSTACKMAP:72 " *      <li>Generator loop process is repeated until all mandatory frames are cleared or until an error state is reached." That is a fixpoint, measured at JDKSTACKMAP:76 " *          <i>(Note: experimental measurements showed that more than 99% of the cases required only single pass to clear all frames," with under 1% needing a second. **Route one also creates a producer obligation that exists only because the checker must reach every instruction.** JDKSTACKMAP:79 " * <li>Dead code patching to pass class loading verification:<ul>" and JDKSTACKMAP:81 " *      <li>Each dead code block is filled with <code>NOP</code> instructions, terminated with" `ATHROW`. The producer rewrites code that cannot run so that the checker has a state to read for it. **3. Route two, and its closure.** LLVM declares the join's type on the join instruction: LLVMLANGREF:13556 "The type of the incoming values is specified with the first type field." positioned so that it is readable at the block head, LLVMLANGREF:13563 "There must be no non-phi instructions between the start of a basic block" and the PHI nodes. Cranelift moves the declaration onto the block: CRANEIR:108 "Cranelift does not have phi instructions but uses [BB parameter]s" CRANEIR:109 "instead. A BB can be defined with a list of typed parameters. Whenever control" CRANEIR:110 "is transferred to the BB, argument values for the parameters must be provided." and the function entry is the same object, CRANEIR:111 "When entering a function, the incoming function parameters are passed as" arguments to the entry BB's parameters. The closure is one sentence: every SSA value is CRANEIR:115 "BB parameters or instruction results.", both of which carry a type, so no environment is ever derived. The verifier reads the declaration back at both ends and derives nothing: CRANEVERIFY:1257 "    fn typecheck_entry_block_params(&self, errors: &mut VerifierErrors) -> VerifierStepResult {" checks the entry block's parameters against the function signature, and CRANEVERIFY:1529 "        for (arg, param) in args.zip(block_params.iter()) {" checks each branch argument against the declared parameter type. Both report non-fatally, which is FD-14's collect-all, and it is affordable for the reason FD-14 gave. The two routes are stated as equivalent in content: CRANECMP:132 "representations are equivalent, but the BB arguments are better suited to handle" blocks reached by several branches with different arguments. **4. WebAssembly is route one over a nesting tree, which is the published shape closest to this tree's `Block`.** The annotation sits on the structured instruction: WASMINSTRSYN:90 "A structured instruction can consume *input* and produce *output* on the operand stack according to its annotated :ref:`block type <syntax-blocktype>`." The single-pass algorithm reads it instead of computing it, WASMVALALG:353 "       case (block t1*->t2*)" then WASMVALALG:355 "         push_ctrl(block, [t1*], [t2*])". The surrounding state is inherited rather than restated, by WASMVALALG:164 "the height of the operand stack at the start of the block (used to check that operands do not underflow the current block)". Every branch is checked against a declared label type, WASMVALALG:375 "       case (br n)" popping `label_types`, where WASMVALALG:268 "     return (if (frame.opcode = loop) frame.start_types else frame.end_types)". The producer's obligation grew when the annotation grew: WASMMULTIVAL:117 "* block types (in `block`, `loop`, `if` instructions) are generalised from *resulttype* to *functype*", so WASMMULTIVAL:129 "* The type of `block`, `loop`, and `if` is the *functype* \[t1\*\] -> \[t2\*\] given as the block type", costing WASMMULTIVAL:148 "The binary requires a change to allow function types as block types. That requires extending the current ad-hoc encoding to allow references to function types." **5. What completeness needs in this tree, measured on the checker.** The tree's blocks nest and never join. `TalTerm` is two forms, `t-ret` and `tt-case` (`lib/lowering/tal/ssa.chiral:38`), there is no jump instruction, and a `Branch` carries a whole nested `Block` (`:39`). A block's entry environment is therefore the enclosing `REnv` at the case, extended by the branch's fields: `lib/lowering/tal/check.chiral:279`, `(ck-block ce (bind-dsts env dsts ftys) body ret)`. The enclosing half is derived by `ck-instrs` (`:225-230`), so one refusal in the enclosing instruction run makes every nested block unreachable to the checker. **The completeness gap is in the walk and not in `Block`.** **6. What each surveyed system would require `Block` to carry.** Under the JVM's discipline `Block` would carry a full register-file type at entry, every live register with its `TalTy`, restated at every block. Under Cranelift's and WebAssembly's it would carry nothing: Cranelift declares what crosses the edge and inherits the rest by dominance, WebAssembly declares `t1*->t2*` and inherits the rest by stack height. **A `tt-case` branch's binding is already the declaration those two want.** `ck-branches` takes `ftys` from `tck-find-ctor` over the scrutinee's constructor (`check.chiral:272-280`), and `DCtor`, `DData` and `CEnv` (`ssa.chiral:48-50`) are artifact data the checker reads rather than invents. The field types crossing into a branch are declared, positionally by `dsts`, in the same way Cranelift's block parameters are. What a branch does not declare is the enclosing environment, and no route-two system declares that either. **7. The three fields, counted.** `Instr` is eight constructors at `ssa.chiral:26-34`; the `(data Instr ()` header is line 26 and the eighth form `i-blen` is line 34, so PRB-75's `:26-33` and FD-17's `:27-34` each miss one end. `i-bput` defines no value. `i-bnew` (`:31`), `i-bget` (`:32`) and `i-blen` (`:34`) each bind a `dst` and carry no `ty`, and `check.chiral:215-218` supplies `(tt-bytes)`, `(tt-i64)` and `(tt-i64)` from the checker's own constants. Those three are the whole of the producer obligation route two would create here. **8. The producer, named.** `compile-fn` at `lib/lowering/upper/lower.chiral:412-420` emits every typed SSA `TFn`. ### FD-20 accepting a target program witnesses target well-typedness alone, and every published route to a preservation claim is a function of two programs

- state:    OPEN
- claim:    The question, for `.planning/TAL-CONFORMANCE-QUEUE.md` slice R6: what does accepting a target program witness, and how do certifying compilers relate the source and the target? **An acceptance witnesses progress and preservation for the target under the target's own type system, and it names no source term. Certifying compilation does not close that gap, because the certificate attests the same target-only safety policy and Necula prices it himself as too coarse to catch an optimizer error. Every published construction that reaches a preservation claim is a function of TWO programs, and the split between them is arity: `Validate(S, C)` and `V : Source x Target -> boolean` take the source and the target, while `ck-prog` takes the target.** Two families reach the claim and they differ in when the relation is discharged. Translation validation discharges it once per compilation, at the price of a validator that is itself untrusted until it is proved. A verified compiler discharges it once over all programs. Both state the relation over semantics for each side and neither mentions a type translation. **So the answer to the total-`ttype` question is a fork, and it orders the queue.** A type-preservation claim of FD-15's published shape puts `[[t]]` in its own conclusion, so the total type translation FD-15 found missing is a precondition of writing the sentence down. A semantic-preservation claim of CompCert's shape names no type translation and requires instead an operational semantics for each side plus a two-argument relation over them. The tree holds one side of that already: `lib/lowering/tal/eval.chiral` is the target's operational semantics at 187 lines with zero importers, which is the object every surveyed validator is proved against.
- measured: **1. What a target-level acceptance witnesses, at TAL's own source.** TAL states the independence as the feature: TALTR:54 "the safety of the resulting assembly code can be checked independently of the source code or" the compiler. What acceptance yields is a property of the target alone, TALTR:1905 "Corollary 6.3 (Type Safety)If|-P, then there is no stuckPsuch thatP|->-->P." No source term occurs in that statement. TALT lists what still has to be trusted for it to mean anything, TALT:75 "One must trust that the TALx86 type checking soft-" ware correctly implements its type system. **2. The certifying compiler attests the same target-only property, and its author says so in the same paragraph.** NECTHESIS:1051 "handle complex safety properties. In contrast, certifying compilation as presented in this" dissertation handles only type safety. The receiver's position is NECTHESIS:2159 "have to trust the certifying compiler because it has other means to verify that the emitted" code has the desired properties, and the limit is stated four lines later: attaching the compiler to the PCC infrastructure does NECTHESIS:2164 "not verify the complete correctness of the compiler, but only that it emits code with certain" properties, such as type safety. **Necula then prices his own certificate against a source-to-target relation and calls it too coarse.** TVPLDI:265 "to verify full semantic equivalence but verifies only that the" output has certain expected properties, and a criterion of that kind, TVPLDI:423 "source is memory safe then so is the target, such as checked" TVPLDI:424 "by the Touchstone certifying compiler) does not allow the" TVPLDI:425 "detection of subtle errors in the optimizer." **3. Every published route to a preservation claim takes two programs, and the arity is the whole difference.** Necula's per-run form: TVPLDI:47 "we cannot prove that a compiler is always correct maybe" we can at least check the correctness of each compilation, and the object carrying it is a relation, TVPLDI:495 "simulation relation is a witness that two program fragments" are equivalent. Pnueli's group states the family identically, VOC:66 "which, after every run" of the compiler a validating tool formally confirms that the target code produced is a correct VOC:68 "translation of the source program.", and TVLOOPS:15 "self, translation validation validates the correctness of" each translation. CompCert types the object, COMPCERTCACM:435 ": a boolean-valued function" `Validate` COMPCERTCACM:439 ") that verifies the property" S ~ C a posteriori, and the two-argument shape is in the shipping code: COMPCERTALLOC:1345 "Definition check_function (rtl: RTL.function) (ltl: LTL.function) (env: regenv): res unit :=". Tristan and Leroy give the type, VALSCHED:99 "it sufces to model the validator as a function" V : Source x Target -> boolean whose truth implies the VALSCHED:114 "desired semantic equivalence result between the source code" and the compiled code. The proved-once alternative carries the same arity, COMPCERTDRV:446 "Theorem transf_c_program_correct:" concluding a backward simulation between the source program's semantics and the target program's, with COMPCERTDRV:419 "Theorem c_semantic_preservation:" as its per-program half. **4. What each addition costs, measured.** An unverified per-run validator: TVPLDI:23 "can be implemented with about the effort typically" TVPLDI:24 "required to implement one compiler pass.", and it buys confidence with no formal guarantee, because COMPCERTCACM:486 "a verified compiler: the validator could itself be incorrect." Closing that costs a proof, COMPCERTCACM:489 "is verified if it is accompanied with a formal proof of the" following property, and the price is on the record for two scheduling optimizations: VALSCHED:4308 "The Coq development accounts for approximatively 11000 lines" VALSCHED:4309 "of code. It took one person-year to design the validators, program" them and prove their correctness. A certificate in place of a relation costs artifact bytes instead: a Popcorn compiler CERTINDEP:1228 "of source code and compiles to 816 kilobytes of object code" carries annotations that naively CERTINDEP:1256 "is over 4.5 megabytes, several times the size of the object" code, and the paper's techniques bring it down so that total annotation size drops from 4.5 CERTINDEP:1337 "megabytes to 419 kilobytes and verification time is reduced" from 59 to 34.5 seconds. The certificate route also leaves a trusted base, FPCC:24 "only if there's no bug in the typing rules, or in the type-" checker or in the assembler; shrinking it is a separate program of work whose whole claim is that the FPCC:110 "trusted base can be smaller: its trusted base consists only" of the foundational verification system, the machine instruction semantics and the safety policy, making foundational proof-FPCC:43 "carrying code is PCC with trusted components an order" FPCC:44 "of magnitude smaller than previous PCC systems." **5. Whether a preservation claim can be stated without a total type translation. Yes for one family and no for the other, and the fork is which relation is preserved.** FD-15 measured the typed statement as five lemmas of the shape `|- e : t` implies `|- [[e]] : [[t]]`. `[[t]]` stands in the conclusion, so a total function on types is a precondition of writing the lemma at all, and nothing in this slice's sources weakens that. The semantic statement mentions no types. It assumes two semantics, COMPCERTCACM:126 "mantics for the source and target languages that associate" observable behaviors to S and C, and the validator is discharged against one of them: VALSCHED:135 "We then prove the correctness of these validators" VALSCHED:136 "against an operational semantics." Necula's validator is untyped throughout and TVPLDI:260 "then uses symbolic evaluation along with constraint solving" over the two intermediate forms. So the typed route needs the total `ttype` at `lib/lowering/upper/lower.chiral:35` that FD-15 measured as partial and non-injective, and the semantic route needs an evaluator for each side. **6. Where `ck-prog` sits against that, structurally.** `ck-prog` is `(-> CEnv Prog TckR)` at `lib/lowering/tal/check.chiral:308`. Both arguments are target-level: `CEnv` at `lib/lowering/tal/ssa.chiral:50` holds `TalSig`s, `DData`s and literals, and `ck-prog` rebuilds its `fns` field out of the `Prog` it was handed (`lib/lowering/tal/check.chiral:312`, `prog-fns`). No `UT` and no `Core` term is in scope. An acceptance is therefore TALTR's Corollary 6.3 over this target and nothing beyond it. **7. The tree has already measured one target program that `ck-prog` accepts and that does not implement its source.** `records/enforcement-arc.md` EN-20, checked 2026-09-04: `arm-body`'s `(none)` arm at `lib/lowering/upper/closconv.chiral:1057` emitted the literal `0` as a whole function body, and on a control fixture whose family codomain is `I64` the row records that `const 0 : i64` matches the declared return, `ck-prog` accepts, and nothing anywhere reddens. The acceptance is the measurement this slice needed, taken inside this tree before the question was asked. **8. What the unreached reference interpreter is worth to the semantic route.** `lib/lowering/tal/eval.chiral` is 187 lines with zero importers, re-measured by PRB-67 on 2026-09-06 and re-run here (`grep -rl 'lowering/tal/eval' --include='*.chiral' lib/ prog/` returns nothing). Its header at `:10` already states a target-only cross-check, no `ck-ok` program evaluates to `r-err`, which is Corollary 6.3 read operationally. That is the object VALSCHED:136 names, and it is the target half of what a `Validate(S, C)` would be stated over; `lib/evidence/interp.chiral` at 109 lines is the source half. `docs/elements/catalog.md:484` (E169) pairs exactly those two files as half (a) and separately calls `preserve-check` "ALREADY a translation validator". **That second reading does not survive the definitions above.** Every validator in these sources is a function of the source and the target, and `ck-prog`'s type admits only the target. **9. What the sources did not settle, and what could not be reached.** Pnueli, Siegel and Singerman's TACAS 1998 original is behind Springer's paywall (`link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/BFb0054170.pdf` returns a 3,038-byte HTML shell) and no open copy was found at `cs.nyu.edu`, `cs.tau.ac.il`, `wisdom.weizmann.ac.il` or `web.archive.org`; `VOC` and `TVLOOPS`, both by Pnueli's group, carry the family's own statement in its place. `people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~necula/` now 302s to a site that returns a 404 wrapper for every paper path, so the PLDI 2000 paper was taken from `web.archive.org`. ## The crypto model

### FD-13 the permutation machine has four slots and a Keccak round has five steps

- state:    OPEN
- claim:    `.planning/CRYPTO-MODEL.md:118-121` says one machine covers Keccak-f and Ascon-p: `rows` rows of 5 lanes of width `w`, an S-box across each row, a linear layer, a round constant, and that the lane permutation "is a function of `rows` and becomes the identity at `rows = 1`", so Ascon's missing step needs no special case. The question: does a Keccak-f round decompose into exactly an S-box across each row, a linear layer, a lane permutation derived from `rows`, and a round constant, such that `rows = 1` yields Ascon-p's round with the lane permutation as the identity and no step left unaccounted for? **No.** The S-box slot and the round-constant slot hold. The four-slot list has no home for the rotation step, and the lane permutation carries no `rows` term to specialize.
- measured: **Five steps, four slots.** FIPS202:15 "A round of a KECCAK-p permutation, denoted by Rnd, consists of a sequence of five transformations, which are called the step mappings", and FIPS202:25 "the round function Rnd is the transformation that results from applying the step mappings , , , , and , in that order" (the five Greek names have no glyph mapping in the extraction and come out empty; KECCAKSUM:179 "# θ step", KECCAKSUM:184 "# ρ and π steps", KECCAKSUM:187 "# χ step" and KECCAKSUM:190 "# ι step" carry them). §4 lists four slots. §5 of the same document counts five: `.planning/CRYPTO-MODEL.md:156` opens "Of the five steps in a Keccak-shaped round" and `:162` names "the rotation layer" as its own row. The model already disagrees with itself two sections apart. **ρ is the step with no slot.** FIPS202:22 "is to rotate the bits of each lane by a length, called the offset, which depends on the fixed x and y coordinates of the lane" is the whole of it. It is intra-lane, one rotation per lane, and it is neither π nor the linear layer. KECCAKSUM:185 "  B[y,2*x+3*y] = rot(A[x,y], r[x,y])," fuses it with π in one assignment, which is where a reading that drops ρ comes from. **π carries no `rows`.** Algorithm 3 is FIPS202:23 "[x, y, z]= A[(x + 3y) mod 5, x, z]", whose effect is FIPS202:23 "is to rearrange the positions of the lanes". The formula has no row-count parameter to instantiate. Its source index at y = 0 is A[x, x], which reads a lane at every y in 0 to 4, so a one-row state has no π to restrict. Read forward from KECCAKSUM:185, a source lane (x, 0) lands at (0, 2x mod 5), scattering row 0 across all five rows. Filling the slot with the identity at `rows = 1` is a legal free choice and it is available. Deriving it from `rows` is the half that fails. **θ and the Σ functions are two shapes under one name.** θ's effect is FIPS202:21 "is to XOR each bit in the state with the parities of two columns in the array", spelled at KECCAKSUM:180 "  C[x] = A[x,0] xor A[x,1] xor A[x,2] xor A[x,3] xor A[x,4]," and KECCAKSUM:181 "  D[x] = C[x-1] xor rot(C[x+1],1),". Ascon's linear layer stays inside one word: ASCONSPEC:77 "s different rotated copies of each word (horizontally, within each word)." and ASCONSPEC:102 "<i>S</i><sub>0</sub> := <i>S</i><sub>0</sub> &oplus; (<i>S</i><sub>0</sub> &#8921; 19) &oplus; (<i>S</i><sub>0</sub> &#8921; 28)". At one row θ's column parity is trivial and the step survives as A[x] ^= A[x-1] xor rot(A[x+1],1), which still crosses lanes, and Ascon has no cross-lane linear step. The step whose position Σ occupies is ρ. Pairing Σ with θ is what leaves ρ homeless, so the mispairing and the missing slot are one defect. **The Keccak-f[1600] and Ascon-p numbers all hold.** Table 1 is FIPS202:15 "b 25 50 100 200 400 800 1600 w 1 2 4 8 16 32 64 l 0 1 2 3 4 5 6"; KECCAKSUM:168 "The state is organized as an array of $5 \times 5$ lanes, each of length $w \in \{1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64\}$ and $b=25w$." gives 25 lanes; KECCAKSUM:171 "is given by $n = 12+2l$, where $2^l = w$. This gives 24 rounds for" gives 24. ASCONSPEC:71 "The round transformation consists of the following three steps which operate on a 320-bit state divided into 5 words" of 64 bits each, and ASCONSPEC:67 "12 rounds in <span class=" names Ascon-p[12]. One qualifier: ASCONSPEC:65 "This permutation iteratively applies an SPN-based round transformation for up to 16 rounds;" and 8 rounds are standardized as Ascon-p[8], so 12 is one of two standardized round counts. **Keccak-f[800] does not arrive free.** `:135` says it "arrives free as `rows = 5, w = 32`" while the machine's rounds row at `:127` carries 24. Table 1 gives l = 5 for b = 800, and FIPS202:26 "KECCAK-f [b] = KECCAK-p[b, 12 + 2l]." puts Keccak-f[800] at 22 rounds. Changing `rows` and `w` alone produces 24 rounds and a different permutation. Round count is a function of `w`, and the machine carries it as an independent type index. **What holds.** The S-box slot: KECCAKSUM:188 "  A[x,y] = B[x,y] xor ((not B[x+1,y]) and B[x+2,y])," varies x at fixed y, and χ's effect is FIPS202:24 "is to XOR each bit with a non-linear function of two other bits in its row"; ASCONSPEC:76 "applies a 5-bit S-box 64 times in parallel in a bit-sliced fashion (vertically, across words)." One bitsliced 5-bit S-box across five lanes, both sides, exactly as `:108-110` claims. The round-constant slot: KECCAKSUM:191 "  A[0,0] = A[0,0] xor RC" against ASCONSPEC:75 "s a round-specific 1-byte constant to word <i>S</i><sub>2</sub>.", and FIPS202:25 "Algorithm 5: rc(t)" is the LFSR derivation `:130` names. Same shape, different lane. **Terminology.** FIPS 202 calls the 5-lane sub-array at fixed y a plane and reserves "row" for a 5-bit sub-array at fixed y and z. §4's "rows of 5 lanes" are FIPS 202's planes. A naming collision with no effect on the finding. **Not settled.** NIST SP 800-232 was fetched (HTTP 200, 1,194,488 bytes) and could not be read here: this sandbox has no `pdftotext` and no PDF library, and the document draws its body text from CID-keyed fonts with hex strings, so the heuristic extractor that produced the FIPS 202 pin returns font tables. The Ascon claims therefore rest on the designers' specification page, which names SP 800-232 as the standard. The Ascon v1.2 submission PDF does extract, and it loses inter-word spacing and maps the Σ glyph to S, so `:129`'s name "the Σ functions" is unverified against a pinned source. The step it names is pinned at ASCONSPEC:77 and ASCONSPEC:102.

## Attribution across a pass that creates definitions

### FD-21 no surveyed system holds one total per-definition attribution across a creating pass, and all six are two-level with the created definition carrying its own identity

- state:    OPEN
- claim:    The question, for E184's decision 1 and R6: when a compiler pass creates or destroys definitions between the point an attribution's domain is fixed and the point the artifact is emitted, what is the domain of a per-definition attribution, and how do published systems keep that attribution total across the pass? **Six systems were read at their own sources: DWARF 5, the TC39 source map standard, LLVM's debug-info rules, LLVM's machine outliner, GHC's cost centres, and AutoFDO. Not one of them carries a single total function from a pre-pass definition set into one closed sum. Every one is two-level. Level one is an entity the artifact contains, level two is an entity the source declared, and a created definition enters level one with its OWN identity plus a typed field naming its origin where an origin exists. The two levels carry different constructors, so a created definition is never a value of the same sum as the definition it came from, and the relation between them is a field on the created entity.** **They then split on which level the attribution ranges over, and the discriminator is measurable: whether the consumer has to name a source entity the artifact no longer contains.** A debugger does, so DWARF keeps both levels and keeps an abstract instance root that has zero concrete instances. A profile that feeds back into the same compiler does not, so AutoFDO fixes the domain at the source level and makes the compiler re-create the pass's creations until the two agree, discarding whatever fails to match. Source maps and the machine outliner take the artifact alone and mark the unattributable. GHC has shipped BOTH domains as two flags and states the price of each in its own manual. **One system implements E184's R1 shape exactly, and its domain is the post-pass set.** LLVM annotates every instruction that has no source location with one of four named values and makes an unannotated absence detectable by a build mode, which is a closed sum with the no-origin arms spelled and no silent arm. **So E184's option (i), the pre-pass set alone as the domain of a total per-definition sum, has no occupant in this survey, and the two occupied shapes are (ii) and (iii).**
- measured: **1. DWARF's domain is the artifact, the source definition survives as a second kind of entry, and the relation is a field.** The source-level definition becomes an abstract instance root, DWARF5:5894 "AnysubroutineentrythatcontainsaDW_AT_inlineattributewhosevalueis" other than DW_INL_not_inlined. Each copy in the artifact is a separate entry, DWARF5:5964 "Eachinlineexpansionofasubroutineisrepresentedbyadebugginginformation" DWARF5:5966 "entrywiththetagDW_TAG_inlined_subroutine." and the back-link is a field on the copy, DWARF5:6070 "entryhasaDW_AT_abstract_originattributethatmaybeusedtoobtainthe" missing information from the associated abstract instance entry. **The cardinality is stated and it is neither one nor onto.** DWARF5:6056 "Anygivenabstractinstancetreemaybe" DWARF5:6058 "associatedwithseveraldifferentconcreteinlinedinstancetrees,ormayevenbeassociated" DWARF5:6060 "withzeroconcreteinlinedinstancetrees." A definition with zero surviving copies keeps its entry, which is the case E184 §1 M-D measures for a pruned `x64`. **2. DWARF names the created-with-no-origin case and gives it its own arm.** DWARF5:6148 "3.Aconcreteinstancetreemaycontainentrieswhichdonotcorrespondto" entries in the abstract instance tree, to describe new entities specific to a particular expansion, and those entries DWARF5:6154 "entriesintheabstractinstancetree,donotcontainDW_AT_abstract_origin" attributes and must contain all their own attributes directly. That is E184 option (ii)'s `ft-created` arm, in a published standard, as the arm for a name with no pre-pass existence. **3. DWARF splits the creators by mechanism and gives each its own construct, so a single arm does not cover them.** An out-of-line copy of an inlinable subroutine reuses the origin field, DWARF5:6188 "concreteout-of-lineinstancemakesuseofDW_AT_abstract_originattributesin" exactly the same way, and differs in tag and in ownership, DWARF5:6214 "treesbeownedbythesameparententry." A compiler-created intermediary gets a different attribute entirely, DWARF5:6270 "Atrampolineisacompiler-generatedsubroutinethatservesasanintermediaryin" making a call to another subroutine, represented by a subprogram entry with a DWARF5:6280 "DW_AT_trampolineattribute.Thevalueofthatattributeindicatesthetarget" subroutine of the trampoline. LLVM emits exactly that for a created global whose name is the original plus a suffix, `sub1_.t0p` beside `sub1_`, and LLVMDBG:1431 "The targetFuncName field is the name of the function that the trampoline" calls. **This is the direct answer to whether `specialize-singletons` and `outline` take one arm or two: DWARF gives three mechanisms three constructs, and the discriminator is what the created entity stands in for.** **4. Source maps range over the generated file and make the unattributable position a representable shape.** The mapped-from side is defined as SRCMAP:257 "code which is generated by the compiler or transpiler." and a mapping segment is SRCMAP:794 "each segment is made up of 1, 4, or 5 variable length fields." The one-field shape is the created case: SRCMAP:807 "Segments with one field are intended to represent generated code that is unmapped because there is no corresponding original source code" SRCMAP:807 "such as code that is generated by a compiler." The standard states no totality requirement over generated positions, so a generated position may carry no segment at all, and the format cannot tell that case from a position nobody mapped. **5. LLVM is the one surveyed system that spells R1's shape, and it spells it over the post-pass set.** The guarantee is stated over the artifact, LLVMDBG:92 "the source-level state of the program**, regardless of which LLVM" optimizations have been run, and it is priced in accuracy for sampled profiles, LLVMDBG:72 "Maintaining" LLVMDBG:73 "deterministic and distinct source locations is necessary to maximize the" accuracy of mapping hardware sample counts to LLVM IR. The rule for a created instruction is a closed set of named reasons: LLVMDBGUP:166 "Whenever a new instruction is created and there is no suitable location for that" instruction, that instruction should be annotated accordingly, from a set LLVMDBGUP:168 "of special `DebugLoc` values that can be set on an instruction to annotate the" reason it has no valid location. The four are compiler-generated, LLVMDBGUP:172 "compiler-generated instruction, i.e. it is not associated with any user source" code; dropped, LLVMDBGUP:175 "intentionally had its source location removed, according to the rules for" dropping locations; unknown, LLVMDBGUP:179 "a known or currently knowable source location, e.g. that it is infeasible to" determine; and temporary, for instructions not expected to be emitted. **The silent arm is the one thing the design refuses.** A build LLVMDBGUP:190 "built with coverage-tracking" keeps track of these special locations LLVMDBGUP:192 "these special locations in order to detect unintentionally-missing locations;" and the manual's own reason for preferring an absence over a wrong annotation is LLVMDBGUP:194 "an absent location can be detected" and fixed. That is R1's no-`_`-arm requirement with a checker behind it, at instruction granularity, over the code the artifact contains. **6. LLVM's machine outliner is the published pass closest to this tree's `outline`, and its created definition gets an entry with no origin field and a dropped interior.** The created name is generated by the pass, LLVMOUTLINER:893 "  // Create the function name. This should be unique." and the scheme is a counter suffix the source calls unstable, LLVMOUTLINER:894 "  // FIXME: We should have a better naming scheme. This should be stable," regardless of changes to the outliner's cost model, built as LLVMOUTLINER:899 "  FunctionName += std::to_string(Name);". The body's attribution is discarded deliberately: LLVMOUTLINER:950 "    // Don't keep debug information for outlined instructions." with `auto DL = DebugLoc();` set on every duplicated instruction. The created function itself enters the domain as its own subprogram, LLVMOUTLINER:1002 "  // If there's a DISubprogram associated with this outlined function, then" emit debug info for it, built at LLVMOUTLINER:1017 "        0 /* Line 0 is reserved for compiler-generated code. */," and flagged LLVMOUTLINER:1020 "        DINode::DIFlags::FlagArtificial /* Compiler-generated code. */,". **No `DW_AT_abstract_origin` is set on it**, which is consistent with DWARF's rule, because LLVM's outliner merges N candidate sites into one function and no single origin exists. **This tree's `outline` (`lib/lowering/upper/lower.chiral:311-320`) extracts one case from one definition, so it has exactly one origin and DWARF's out-of-line-instance construct fits it where LLVM's outliner does not.** **7. GHC has shipped both domains, and its manual states the price of each.** The early domain is `-fprof-auto`: GHCPROF:204 "to the compiler, it automatically inserts a cost centre annotation" around every binding not marked INLINE, and the price is the passes, GHCPROF:207 "cost-centre annotations as the optimiser is careful to not move them around or" remove them, which can severely affect how the program is optimised. The late domain is `-fprof-late`: GHCPROF:499 "This is done late in the compilation pipeline after the optimizer has run and unfoldings have been created." and the price is stated in the next paragraph, GHCPROF:504 "While the results of this are generally informative, some of the compiler internal names" GHCPROF:505 "will leak into the profile." The created-name shape is this tree's exactly, a suffixed global with no source counterpart: cost centres added after simplification mean the names differ from the source, GHCPROF:418 "they appear in the source program (e.g. a call to " `f` may be inlined with GHCPROF:419 "    its wrapper, resulting in an occurrence of its worker, " `$wf`. The pass code exists as its own module, GHCLATECC:3 "-- | Adds cost-centers after the core pipline has run." **GHC also measures the case where a pass creates top-level definitions and the attribution gives up on distinguishing them.** Full laziness lifts constants out of function bodies, GHCPROF:316 "and higher), as constants in function bodies will be lifted to the top-level" GHCPROF:317 "and become CAFs. You will probably need to consult the Core" to determine what these CAFs correspond to, and the default attribution for all of them is one shared bucket, GHCPROF:311 "assigns every CAF in a module a stack consisting of the single cost" centre `M.CAF`. So the created definitions get a catch-all until a flag gives each its own, and even then their relation back to source is left to a human reading the intermediate dump. **8. The published lambda-lifting treatment carries the mapping inside the pass, and the lifted definition is a new name whose source binding is consumed.** Graf and Peyton Jones state the operational consequences as a numbered list: the transformation SELLAM:353 "Itcreatesanewtop-levelde" finition `f` with a mark, replaces the `let` by its body, and rewrites every occurrence at the call sites. The pass threads the relation explicitly, SELLAM:1071 "5.1VariablesInthevariablecase,wecheckifthevariablewasli" fted to top-level by looking it up in the supplied expander mapping. They attribute the construction to SELLAM:307 "Johnsson(1985)introducedit" for efficient code generation of lazy functional languages to G-machine code. **This is the one surveyed source whose shape matches R6's prescription of a mapping produced by the pass and carried onward, and the object it maps is a LOCAL binding that the transformation consumes**, so the original has no separate fate to keep. `lift-lifted` (`lib/lowering/upper/specialize-singleton.chiral:195`) lifts a field body out of a global that `prune-live` (`:227`) keeps whenever something still references it, which is the case lambda lifting does not have. **9. AutoFDO makes the domains agree instead of making the attribution total, and it discards the residue.** The attribution unit is a source location annotated with an inline stack, AUTOFDO:78 "otherentriesrepresentthesourcelocationsoftheinlined" call sites, and the database is a forest, AUTOFDO:156 "leisorganizedasaforestoftrees" whose AUTOFDO:161 "Innernodesinatreerepresent" AUTOFDO:162 "functioninlineinstances.Leaftreenodesrepresentsource" statements. All instances of one function AUTOFDO:420 "(inlinedorstandalone)arerepresentedbydifferentsubtrees." The reconciliation is a pass that re-performs the creations: the preparation AUTOFDO:423 "steptransformstheIRandmakesitresembletheinlinetree" structure stored in the profile, after which AUTOFDO:510 "eachoneofthenewlycreatedinlineinstanceshasexactly" one matching inner node in the profile tree. What fails to match is dropped: the profile AUTOFDO:516 "samplesfromcoldinstancesthatarenotinlined" AUTOFDO:517 "duringthepreparationsteparediscarded." So the totality AutoFDO gets is bought by re-running the creating pass under the profile's control, and the attribution itself stays partial. **10. What the survey says about R6's premise, which E184 §1 M-D already refuted from the source.** No surveyed system carries a rename mapping, because no surveyed pass renames. DWARF, LLVM and GHC all give a created definition a new identity in the artifact's own namespace and relate it to its origin through a field or a tag, and DWARF keeps the original entry even when the artifact contains nothing of it. **R6's "fates are a relation across a renaming" has no occupant in this survey; the occupied shape is a relation across a creation, with the created entity in the domain.** This row records the contradiction and amends nothing. **11. What the survey does not settle.** No source states a conservation obligation of R7's shape, that folding the attribution reproduces the emitted set and a missing or doubled entry fails the build. LLVM's coverage-tracking mode is the nearest and it detects a missing annotation without failing the compilation. Nothing surveyed prices the cost of computing the domain in two stages, which is E184 option (ii)'s stated cost. And nothing surveyed decides whether a definition that survives a pass and is also the origin of a created one takes one arm or two, because DWARF's abstract instance root sits in a different sum from the arms a concrete instance carries. **12. What could not be reached.** Johnsson's "Lambda Lifting: Transforming Programs to Recursive Equations" (FPCA 1985, LNCS 201, pages 190 to 203) is behind Springer's paywall: `link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/3-540-15975-4_37` returns a 231,292-byte HTML shell with HTTP 200, and no open copy was found. Graf and Peyton Jones' ICFP 2019 paper is pinned in its place and carries the attribution to Johnsson. `llvm/docs/SourceLevelDebugging.rst` and `llvm/docs/HowToUpdateDebugInfo.rst` both return HTTP 404 at `main`, because the LLVM docs moved to Markdown; the `.md` paths were pinned. The DWARF 5 PDF was pinned as a transcription for the reason recorded in `evidence:` below.
- evidence: Ten pins added 2026-09-09 in `.planning/sources/`. **Seven are origin `raw`**: `SRCMAP` (ECMA-426, the TC39 Source map format specification, `spec.emu` at `github.com/tc39/ecma426`, which renders to `tc39.es/ecma426/`; the rendered HTML was fetched first at 568,647 bytes and rejected as a pin because its inline scripts put the normative text on lines shared with minified JavaScript), `LLVMDBG` and `LLVMDBGUP` (`llvm/docs/SourceLevelDebugging.md` and `llvm/docs/HowToUpdateDebugInfo.md`), `LLVMOUTLINER` (`llvm/lib/CodeGen/MachineOutliner.cpp`), `CLANGUSERS` (`clang/docs/UsersManual.md`, pinned for the sample-profile build cycle at CLANGUSERS:3097 "DWARF information can be improved with the `-fdebug-info-for-profiling`" and not otherwise quoted), `GHCPROF` (`docs/users_guide/profiling.rst`) and `GHCLATECC` (`compiler/GHC/Core/LateCC.hs`). **Three are origin `transcribed`**, because this sandbox has no PDF library and the text is a stdlib zlib-plus-content-stream extraction: `DWARF5` (DWARF Debugging Information Format Version 5, February 13 2017, `dwarfstd.org/doc/DWARF5.pdf`), `SELLAM` (Graf and Peyton Jones, "Selective Lambda Lifting", ICFP 2019, `arxiv.org/pdf/1910.11717`) and `AUTOFDO` (Chen, Li and Moseley, "AutoFDO: Automatic Feedback-Directed Optimization for Warehouse-Scale Applications", CGO 2016, `research.google.com/pubs/archive/45290.pdf`). ### FD-22 the tree's only shipping attribution consumer reads exclusively the population the post-pass domain deletes, and the published price of the retained level is artifact bytes this element never writes

- state:    OPEN
- claim:    The question, for E184's decision 1 as amended: when an attribution's consumer must name entities the emitted artifact does not contain, what does each published domain choice cost that consumer, and what does it cost the producer to keep the pre-pass entities addressable? **Twelve further sources were read at their own sources, and the answer has two halves.** **The consumer half is lopsided.** Every published consumer that must name a source entity the artifact lost pays for it with a second retained level, and each one states its own failure when that level is missing: `gdb` cannot place a breakpoint at an inlined call site because the site holds no code, and LLVM's coverage tool cannot tell an unreachable line from an executed one because it does not hold the frontend's knowledge. E184's consumer is on that side, and this run measures it rather than assuming it: `blame-chain` and `format-blame` are the only shipping readers of the attribution, they key on `def-name`, and all **347** records they read name definitions that produced no artifact entity. Under **(iii)** those 347 leave the domain, and with them three of R1's four arms lose every member they have, leaving `emitted` alone and turning one total function into one sum plus two side relations. **The producer half is balanced and it goes the other way.** The published price of keeping the pre-pass level addressable is artifact size, measured once by Fission at **87%** of object-file bytes and **84%** of binary bytes for the whole of debug information. E184's conformance row 4 pins every emitted ELF byte-identical, so the attribution ships no bytes and that price does not transfer; what **(ii)** costs here is a two-stage domain and a wider fold, against the fact that **(iii) is the shape of the code as it stands**, which threads `skips` beside `acc` in two channels today. **The sub-question splits two to one with one abstention, and the majority answer is ONE arm carrying a mechanism tag.** GCC gives every creating mechanism one construct, an origin pointer plus a `SUFFIX` string, and its function-splitting pass is `outline`'s near twin under that one construct. MLIR discriminates by the arity of the origin set and not by the mechanism. DWARF gives three mechanisms three constructs. LLVM's machine outliner does not reach the case. **No option is dominated and the ruling stays the author's.**
- measured: **1. THE DISCRIMINATOR APPLIED TO THIS TREE, VERIFIED AT HEAD `6e725c3` RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** R1's four arms and their populations, read from `docs/decisions/decision-def-partition.md:104-118` and not re-derived: `emitted` **22,395 of 22,742** across 63 roots; `skipped` **347**, in three producing channels (`body-does-not-lower` 182 at `compile-back.chiral:271`, `callee-cascade` 160 at `prune-pass`, `extern-with-no-wrapper` 5 at `filter-erasable`); `erased-by-design` **0**; `specialized-into` **unmeasured**. Three of the four name definitions with no emitted artifact entity. **The tree's only shipping consumer of the attribution reads those three and nothing else.** `SkRec` is `(mk-skrec (def-name Str) (why SkReason))` at `lib/lowering/skip-diag.chiral:16`; `blame-chain` (`:92`) keys the walk on `def-name` and `skwhy-name`; `format-blame` (`:119-121`) renders the chain and is what E187's R5 gates byte-for-byte. Every one of the 347 records exists because a definition produced no `TFn`. **347 of 347 sit on FD-21's "must name" side of the discriminator, and 0 of 347 name an entity the artifact contains.** That is the measurement FD-21 stopped short of.
  **2. WHAT THE CONSUMERS ON THAT SIDE NEED, STATED BY THEIR OWN DOCUMENTATION.** A debugger needs the producer to have kept the lost entity: GDBINLINE:82 "For <small>GDB</small> to support inlined functions, the compiler must" GDBINLINE:83 "record information about inlining in the debug information". A symbolizer reconstructs entities that carry no symbol: LLVMSYMBOLIZE:333 "If a source code location is in an inlined function, prints all the inlined" frames. A profiler does the same on the call graph and does it by default: PERFREPORT:606 "	If a callgraph address belongs to an inlined function, the inline stack" will be printed, PERFREPORT:608 "	default, disable with --no-inline." **And `gdb` states the failure that arrives when the named entity is absent from the artifact.** GDBINLINE:110 "Setting breakpoints at the call site of an inlined function may not" GDBINLINE:111 "work, because the call site does not contain any code." and GDBINLINE:117 "cannot locate the return value of inlined calls after" using `finish`, which the manual files as GDBINLINE:119 "debugging information; after <code>finish</code>" a limitation of what the compiler emitted. **A consumer that must name an absent entity degrades in named ways, and the manual names them.**
  **3. THE COVERAGE CONSUMER FIXES ITS DOMAIN BEFORE THE OPTIMIZER RUNS, AND SAYS WHY.** The producer is the frontend: LLVMCOVMAP:60 "For each function that requires code coverage, the frontend has to create" LLVMCOVMAP:61 "coverage mapping data that can map between the source code ranges and" the profile instrumentation counters. **The format carries a region kind whose whole job is a source range with no artifact entity.** LLVMCOVMAP:90 "* Skipped regions are used to represent source ranges that were skipped" LLVMCOVMAP:91 "  by Clang's preprocessor. They don't associate with" counters, and LLVMCOVMAP:93 "  executed. They are used by the code coverage tool to mark the skipped lines" inside a function as non-code lines. It is a numbered arm in the encoding, LLVMCOVMAP:561 "  * 2 - This mapping region is a skipped region." **This is E184's `skipped` arm in a shipped format, and its domain is the pre-pass source set by construction.** The document also states, in one sentence, what is lost when the domain is fixed later: without the frontend's zero counters the tool would think unreachable lines were executed, LLVMCOVMAP:220 "as it doesn't possess the frontend's knowledge." **The consumer cannot reconstruct what the producer knew and discarded.**
  **4. THE PUBLISHED PRICE OF THE RETAINED LEVEL IS ARTIFACT SIZE, IT IS MEASURED ONCE, AND IT IS MEASURED FOR THE WHOLE OF DEBUG INFORMATION.** Fission exists for one reason, DEBUGFISSION:137 "project was started in response to the problems caused by huge amounts of debug information in large applications". The figure: DEBUGFISSION:141 "the debug information accounts for 87% of the total size of the object files sent as inputs to the link step, and 84% of the total size of the output binary", for a large C++ application at `-O2 -g`. The breakdown puts the entries themselves at DEBUGFISSION:143 "Debug Information Entries - .debug_info (11%)" of object-file size, with relocations at 46%. **This measures the retained source level as a whole and isolates nothing.** No source read in this run measures debug-info size attributable to abstract instance roots specifically, and that is what the tree would need to price DWARF's retention directly.
  **5. DWARF STATES WHAT THE RETAINED ROOT IS AND STATES THE MECHANISM THAT HOLDS ITS COST DOWN.** The abstract instance root is an entity with no runtime existence, by the standard's own words: DWARF5:5944 "sincesuchentriesdonotrepresentactual(concrete)instancesandthusdonotactually" exist at run-time. The cost is amortized by sharing, DWARF5:5922 "Attributesandchildreninanabstractinstancearesharedbyallconcrete" instances, and the copies pay only their difference, DWARF5:6062 "Concreteinlinedinstanceentriesmayomitattributesthatarenot" specific to the concrete instance. The standard also grants an explicit omission for the case where the retained level would not be read: DWARF5:6158 "abstractinstancetreetoomitdebugginginformationentriesforanonymous" entities that are unlikely to be needed in most inlined expansions. **So the second level is priced as shared storage and the standard leaves the producer a way to drop the part nobody reads.**
  **6. E184's CONSUMER IS INSIDE THE COMPILE, SO THE PRICED COST DOES NOT TRANSFER.** `docs/examples/E184-def-fate-sum.md` §6 conformance row 4 requires every emitted ELF to stay byte-identical, so the attribution reaches no artifact and pays none of section 4's bytes. **What (ii) costs this tree instead is a fold and a two-stage domain**, and R7's own open question 2 already prices the fold at 22,742 records on every build. The created set adds to that: 13 lifted globals plus 40 outlined extras is **53 on `prog/compiler.prog`**, and across the 63 roots it is unmeasured, which is `docs/examples/E184-def-fate-sum.md` §1 M-D's F3.
  **7. THE PUBLISHED COMPILER-INTERNAL ATTRIBUTIONS THAT ARE NOT DEBUG INFO ARE LOGS, AND GCC SHIPS A CREATE-AND-DESTROY RECORD WITH A NAMED CONSUMER.** GCCDEVOPTS:520 "Create a dump file containing information about creation of call graph" GCCDEVOPTS:521 "node clones and removals of call graph nodes during inter-procedural" GCCDEVOPTS:522 "optimizations and transformations.  Its main intended use is that tools" GCCDEVOPTS:523 "that create live-patches can determine the set of functions that need to" be live-patched to completely replace a particular function. **That is R6's relation and R7's create-and-destroy account, published, with the compile itself as the consumer.** The create record is one line per clone, GCCCLONES:329 "Dump information about creation of a call graph node clone to the dump file" GCCCLONES:330 "created by the -fdump-ipa-clones option.  ORIGINAL is the function being" cloned, emitted as GCCCLONES:345 "	       "Callgraph clone;%s;%d;%s;%d;%d;%s;%d;%s;%d;%d;%s\n"," which is origin name, uid, file, line, column, then the clone's four, then the suffix. The destroy record is one line per removal, GCCCGRAPH:2269 "	     "Callgraph removal;%s;%d;%s;%d;%d\n", asm_name (), get_uid (),". ⚑ **AND IT IS PARTIAL BY CONSTRUCTION, WHICH IS THE POINT FOR R7.** The removal line is guarded: GCCCGRAPH:2267 "  if (symtab->ipa_clones_dump_file && symtab->cloned_nodes.contains (this))", and `cloned_nodes` is populated only where a clone was dumped, GCCCLONES:354 "        symtab->cloned_nodes.add (original);". **A function removed without ever having been cloned leaves no record at all.** The nearest published occupant of R7's conservation obligation is a log restricted to the entities one pass touched, and it neither folds to the emitted set nor fails the build. FD-21 item 11 recorded that nothing surveyed states R7's obligation; this run finds the nearest occupant and measures its partiality.
  **8. LLVM's OPTIMIZATION REMARKS ARE THE OTHER ONE, AND THEY ARE EVENT-KEYED AND OPT-IN.** LLVMREMARKS:6 "LLVM is able to emit diagnostics from passes describing whether an optimization" LLVMREMARKS:7 "has been performed or missed for a particular reason, which should give more" insight into what the compiler did. The serialized record carries LLVMREMARKS:167 "Pass: <pass>" and LLVMREMARKS:170 "Function: <function>" with a `DebugLoc`, and its type is a closed set, LLVMREMARKS:177 "The following entries are mandatory:" beginning LLVMREMARKS:179 "- `<TYPE>`: can be `Passed`, `Missed`, `Analysis`," `AnalysisFPCommute`, `AnalysisAliasing`, `Failure`. **The sum is closed and the domain is a transformation event.** Nothing makes it total over definitions, and the filter is a regex over pass names, LLVMREMARKS:113 "Only passes whose name match the given (POSIX) regular expression will be" LLVMREMARKS:114 "serialized to the final output." **A per-definition fate cannot be recovered from it, because a definition no pass reported is indistinguishable from one no pass touched.**
  **9. MLIR IS A SECOND OCCUPANT OF R1's NO-`_`-ARM CLAUSE AT ENTITY GRANULARITY, AND ITS PASS-LEVEL RECORD IS AN EVENT STREAM.** MLIRLOC:324 "Source location information is an extremely integral part of the MLIR" MLIRLOC:325 "infrastructure. As such, location information is always present in the IR," MLIRLOC:326 "and must explicitly be set to unknown. Thus, an instance of the `unknown`" location represents an unspecified source location. **That is R1's requirement stated as an invariant of the IR rather than as a checker over it**, and it is the second occupant after LLVM's coverage-tracking build. Its pass machinery carries no per-entity account: MLIRPASS:1035 "MLIR provides a customizable framework to instrument pass execution and analysis" MLIRPASS:1036 "computation, via the `PassInstrumentation` class. This class provides hooks into" MLIRPASS:1037 "the PassManager that observe various events:", and the events are pass-granular, MLIRPASS:1048 "This callback is run right after a pass has been successfully executed." beside MLIRPASS:1051 "This callback is run right after a pass execution fails." **So MLIR splits the two jobs: the per-entity attribution is an always-present location on the entity, and the pass record is an observer stream that never claims to be total.**
  **10. THE SUB-QUESTION, ANSWERED FROM THE SOURCES. TWO PUBLISHED ANSWERS SAY ONE ARM, ONE SAYS TWO, ONE ABSTAINS.** **GCC says ONE.** Every creating mechanism goes through one construct with one origin pointer, GCCCLONES:494 "  new_node->clone_of = this;", and the mechanism travels as a parameter of that construct, GCCCLONES:331 "cloned, CLONE is the new clone.  SUFFIX is a string that helps identify the" GCCCLONES:332 "reason for cloning, often it is the suffix used by a particular IPA pass to" GCCCLONES:333 "create unique function names.  SUFFIX can be NULL and in that case the" dumping does not take place. **GCC's function-splitting pass is `outline`'s near twin and it uses that one construct.** GCCSPLIT:21 "/* The purpose of this pass is to split function bodies to improve" inlining, producing GCCSPLIT:34 "   func.part (...)" holding the big branch while `func` calls it, created at GCCSPLIT:1376 "  /* Now create the actual clone.  */" as GCCSPLIT:1380 "     split_point->split_bbs, split_point->entry_bb, "part");" with one boolean beside it, GCCSPLIT:1382 "  node->split_part = true;". **This tree's `outline` (`lib/lowering/upper/lower.chiral:311-320`, re-read at HEAD) does the same shape**: it builds `<name>$<ncase>`, emits `(i-call nreg <name>$<ncase> …)` back in the parent at `:318`, and returns the extra through `st-extra`. **MLIR says ONE, and discriminates on a different axis.** A single origin takes a name wrapped around a child location, MLIRLOC:210 "An instance of this location allows for attaching a name to a child location."; many origins take a tuple, MLIRLOC:171 "An instance of a `fused` location represents a grouping of several other" MLIRLOC:172 "source locations, with optional metadata that describes the context of the" fusion, written for exactly the case where MLIRLOC:174 "may be fused together, e.g. pattern rewriting, that normally result partial" MLIRLOC:175 "or even total loss of location information. With `fused` locations, this is" a non-issue. **MLIR's discriminator is the ARITY of the origin set and the mechanism is metadata.** **DWARF says TWO**, giving three mechanisms three constructs, which is FD-21 item 3 and is read here rather than re-derived. **LLVM's machine outliner abstains**, because it merges N sites and sets no origin field, which is FD-21 item 6. **Both of this tree's creators have exactly one origin.** `lift-lifted` (`lib/lowering/upper/specialize-singleton.chiral:195`, re-read at HEAD) builds `<gname>$<i>` from one field body of one global; `outline` builds `<name>$<ncase>` from one case of one definition. **So arity does not separate them and only the mechanism does**, which puts them on one arm under GCC's and MLIR's shapes and on two under DWARF's. ⚑ **One caveat the tree owes itself: GCC's mechanism tag is a `const char *` and MLIR's fusion metadata is an open attribute, and E184's R2 forbids a `Str` standing for a relation.** The majority answer is one arm carrying a mechanism tag, and the tag's spelling is this tree's own problem.

### FD-23 five principle-holders were read and four of the five put the created entity in the domain under its own identity, the fifth deleted it from the artifact instead, and the one unanimous result is that no holder folds a created entity's account into its origin's

- state:    OPEN
- claim:    The question, for E184's decision 1 and framed by commitment rather than by job: among systems that hold one of chirality's principles as a hard design commitment, what does that commitment force about the domain of a total claim when a transformation creates or destroys the entities the claim ranges over? **Five holders were read at their own sources: seL4's binary verification for P1, CakeML for P2, Fuchsia's component framework for P3, Rust's monomorphization and symbol scheme for P4, and Alive2 with Necula's validator for P5. The pieces AGREE on exactly one thing and it is the strongest result in the run: not one of the five attributes a created entity's property to the definition it came from. Four give the created entity a place of its own; the fifth removes it from the artifact side of the claim so that the domain never has to move. That is E184 option (i) refuted from five further directions, and it does not separate (ii) from (iii).** **The pieces DISAGREE on whether the domain widens, and the discriminator is measurable: whether the attributed property is determined by the origin's property.** Rust's safety claim keeps the pre-pass domain because a monomorphization is safe if its generic item is, so the created copies are never re-checked. CakeML's name claim widens to the post-pass set because a generated application stub has no source function at all. Fuchsia widens the DECLARED domain to an abstract container that may hold zero instances and refuses to widen it to instances, so an inbound route distributes to every member and an outbound route from a created member is stated to be inexpressible. seL4 narrows the artifact instead of widening the domain, and pays for it with a step the checker is told to trust. **The tree already measured which side of that discriminator it is on**: a created def's fate is not a function of its origin's, so the domain must move, which is what R1's ⚑ and E184 §1 M-D already say. **The sharpest single hit is CakeML, and it is a second occupant for (iii)'s shape that FD-21 did not have**: `make_name_alist` is a total function over the POST-pass location set with a spelled `unknown_clos_fun` arm, its discriminant is a numeric band comparison rather than a string, and the map it feeds is threaded through the whole backend, unioned with each later pass's own created-stub names, and consumed against the emitted sections with a spelled `«NOTFOUND»` default. That is R6's "produced by the pass and carried the rest of the way" and R7's artifact-side fold, shipped, in a verified compiler. **P6 does not exist and this run reports that rather than inventing a holder.**
- measured: **1. P1's HOLDER IS seL4's BINARY VERIFICATION, AND ITS COMMITMENT FORCED IT TO DELETE THE CREATED ENTITY RATHER THAN NAME IT.** The claim is total over a fixed function set, SEL4TV:115 "Weprovideafullproofofcorrectnessofthecompilationby" standard gcc 4.5.1 of all previously formally verified functions in seL4 at optimisation level 1. **The entity sets on the two sides do not match, and the paper measures the mismatch rather than assuming it away.** SEL4TV:1765 "Thereare540functionsinseL4,butfarlesssymbolsinthe" binary after inlining. P3's HOLDER IS FUCHSIA, AND ITS COMMITMENT FORCED AN ABSTRACT ROOT THAT MAY HAVE ZERO INSTANCES.** The case is stated as the reason collections exist: dynamic children support uses FUCHSIAREALM:5881 "where the existence or cardinality of component instances cannot be determined" FUCHSIAREALM:5882 "in advance. ## The width of a refusal report

### FD-24 no surveyed report type mirrors its source language's constructor set, and every mirror that is mechanically checked is either inside one module or generated from one table both tiers read

- state:    OPEN

The practice CONVERGES on one result and SPLITS on a second, and the two results answer different halves of the fork.** **The convergent result: not one surveyed report type mirrors its source language's constructor set.** GHC's `HsSyn` carries 321 data constructors and its `TcRnMessage` carries 251, in no correspondence; Go's `go/ast` has 53 node types and its type checker 145 error codes; rustc's const evaluator refuses the whole of MIR through a 7-arm sum naming no MIR form; Cranelift's entire code generator reports through 6 arms of which one is a `Str`; CompCert's verified pipeline reports through 3, none of which names a form. **The one published rule for choosing the width is Go's, and it is keyed on the checker's own refusal sites rather than on the language's grammar**: two errors are one code if a theoretical refactoring of the checker could emit them from exactly one place. **The divergent result is about a mirror the compiler cannot check against its original, which is this tree's actual position, and the four published answers divide on one fact: whether one table can be read from both tiers.** Where it can, the correspondence is GENERATED and the day the source grows is a compile error at the mapping function rather than at either declaration (LLVM's `Instruction.def` textually included into both directions of the C-API opcode mapping; Clang's `tblgen` and its `%enum_select`). Where it cannot, every surveyed system gives up the compile error: Rust's `#[non_exhaustive]` mandates a wildcard outside the defining crate and keeps exhaustiveness inside it, Java's `javax.lang.model` mandates `visitUnknown` and a runtime `UnknownElementException`, Go's `ast.Walk` panics in its default arm, and GHC's own hand-maintained `HsSyn`-against-`TH.Syntax` mirror is described by the authors of both as very difficult to keep in sync. **So exhaustiveness as the enforcement mechanism survives a module boundary and does not survive a tier boundary, in any system read here.** **Applied to E184: the sixteen-arm shape has no occupant in the survey as a REPORT type, and the enforcement it relies on is available in this tree only at the PRODUCER, in `compile-front.chiral`, where `Term` is visible and where the kernel's own exhaustiveness check applies. The two sites that would carry it are the two that today refuse through `_`.** The ruling stays the author's and this row rules nothing.

Omitting this step will lead to hard-to-diagnose" failures regarding matching of template declarations. **That is the silent gap, in the largest surveyed compiler, at exactly the seam the sixteen-arm option exists to close, and nothing in that toolchain catches it.** **GHC's own migration to one constructor per diagnostic is unfinished and the incompleteness is representable in the type**: `diagnosticCode` returns a `Maybe`, GHCERRTYPE:275 "  -- some errors in GHC still use the old system of just writing the" GHCERRTYPE:276 "  -- error message in-place (instead of using a dedicated error type" GHCERRTYPE:277 "  -- and constructor), we do not have error codes for all errors." **GHC also keeps a real catch-all arm in the sum and polices it with a comment rather than with the type**: GHCTCRNTY:329 "  TcRnUnknownMessage :: UnknownDiagnosticFor TcRnMessage -> TcRnMessage", carrying GHCTCRNTY:318 "  -- Please don't use this function inside the GHC codebase;" and GHCTCRNTY:322 "you should add a new constructor to 'TcRnMessage' instead." **Rust's structured-diagnostic refactor produced no closed sum at all.** RUSTDIAGSTRUCT:33 "`Diagnostic` can only be derived on structs and enums." and a diagnostic is one derived struct per error, keyed to a code, RUSTDIAG:76 "Most errors have an associated error code." **A new syntactic form in Rust breaks no diagnostic match, because there is no match to break.** **And GCC answers the refused-form question inside the AST rather than in a report**: GCCTREEDEF:36 "/* Any erroneous construct is parsed into a node of this type." GCCTREEDEF:37 "   This type of node is accepted without complaint in all contexts" GCCTREEDEF:38 "   by later parsing activities, to avoid multiple error messages" for one error, which is Hazel's mark with one arm rather than many.

THIS TREE'S COORDINATES, VERIFIED AT HEAD `4c12958` RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM THE PROMPT.** **The `diag.chiral` precedent is real and it is NOT a mirror of `Term`.** `lib/typing/diag.chiral:324` reads "NO `_` arm, on purpose: a new Reason constructor must break every renderer" loudly, and the sum it guards is `Reason` with 10 arms; the two codes beside it are `Subject` with 12 arms and `Judg` with 36. What the fork turns on is where the correspondence would be checked.**

  **7. THE PUBLISHED POSITION THIS TREE IS IN IS LLVM's, ONE INSTRUMENT SHORT, AND THE SURVEY SAYS SO PRECISELY.** **No surveyed system checks a mirror at the mirror's DECLARATION.** LLVM does not: `LLVMOpcode` and `Instruction.def` are two declarations and neither checks the other. What LLVM checks is the MAPPING, and it checks it by generating the mapping's arms from the source's table. **`SkHead`'s declaration would sit in `skip-diag.chiral` where `Term` is invisible, and its producers would sit in `compile-front.chiral` where `Term` is visible and where the kernel's own exhaustiveness check applies.** That is the same split LLVM has, and the same place the check can live. **The instrument this tree lacks is the shared table**: LLVM's 69 arms and its 69 cases are one list read twice, and sixteen `SkHead` arms with sixteen `Term` cases would be two lists written twice, with only the producer's `case` forcing the second to keep up with the first. **And the exhaustiveness that would force it is disabled today at exactly the two sites that would carry it**, the `_` arms at `compile-front.chiral:72` and `:134`. A producer that keeps a `_` gets the sixteen arms and none of the enforcement they are bought for.

PRB-81 IS EVIDENCE ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE FORK, AND THIS ROW SAYS SO RATHER THAN INHERITING THE FRAMING IT WAS GIVEN.** PRB-81 measures a report type that is too COARSE: `sk-extern` carries all 187 records where 5 are extern refusals, a 97% misattribution on that tag, and the three real body classes have no tag at all (`records/lenses/problems.md` PRB-81, read at HEAD and not re-derived). **That is the failure of under-classification.** Nothing measured in this tree is a mirrored sum drifting from the sum it copied. **The say-it-once tension the fork names is real and it is unmeasured here; the misattribution the three-arm option risks is measured here at 182 records.** Both halves of the fork therefore have evidence and the two halves come from different evidence classes, which is the honest statement of the price.

WHETHER THE PRACTICE CONVERGES OR SPLITS, SAID PLAINLY.** **It converges on the report type**: zero of six surveyed refusal reports mirror a source constructor set, and the one published width rule ranges over emission sites. **It splits on the mirror**, and the discriminator is mechanical rather than stylistic: a mirror inside one module is checked by exhaustiveness; a mirror across a boundary where one table is readable from both tiers is checked by generation; a mirror across a boundary where no such table exists goes unchecked, and all three systems in that position mandate a catch-all and accept a runtime failure. **The direct answer to the fork's last clause: in this survey the mirroring shape is defensible only where the correspondence is mechanically enforced, and it is a finding against sixteen arms at `SkHead`'s declaration site. It is NOT a finding against sixteen arms at the producers, because the producers are in the kernel image, they see `Term`, and the kernel checks exhaustiveness.** Whether that relocation is acceptable is the author's, and the relocation is what E184 decision 3 already puts in front of the author under a different name.

## Where the exhaustiveness obligation sits

### FD-25 the second walk has one surveyed occupant, its two walks are published as disagreeing, and every other surveyed system has the producer leave evidence the classifier only reads

- state:    OPEN

The two placements E184 states are the ends of a three-position spectrum and the surveyed weight sits in the middle.** **The pure second walk, where a classifier re-derives from the same input what the producer already decided, has exactly ONE surveyed occupant: CPython's PEG parser. Its two walks disagree, the implementers say so in their own documentation with a worked example, and the shipped code carries a repair that throws the second walk's answer away and keeps the first walk's.** **At the other end, GHC did retype its producers, and the price is published as prose and as a date: the authors call a single change "highly impractical" for touching a lot of modules, the tracking issue is open since 2020-07-30, and the item that converts the typechecker's own error types is still unticked.** **Between them, two systems put a value at the producer and have the classifier read it: rustc's `ErrorGuaranteed` is a coarse token whose page states it carries no class at all, so nothing a classifier says can contradict it, and GHC's `CtOrigin` is 64 arms of provenance attached where the check happens so the classifier has nothing left to derive.** **The blast radius of placement one in this tree was measured here and nothing recorded it before: 27 call sites, all 27 in `lib/lowering/compile-front.chiral`, spread over 12 enclosing functions, with 3 sites originating a refusal, 19 propagating one, and 3 sinks discarding it.** The ruling stays the author's and this row rules nothing.

What it buys is stated: RUSTERRGUAR:7 "\`ErrorGuaranteed\` is a zero-sized type that is unconstructable outside of the" `rustc_errors` crate, so RUSTERRGUAR:11 "\`ErrorGuaranteed\`, the compilation is _statically guaranteed to fail_." **The answer to why a producer and a classifier here cannot disagree is that the producer says nothing a classifier could contradict**: RUSTERRGUAR:17 "* It does _not_ convey information about the _kind_ of error." **The type system carries the token and no class**: RUSTTYSTY:524 "    pub fn new_error(tcx: TyCtxt<'tcx>, guar: ErrorGuaranteed) -> Ty<'tcx> {" makes a refused type into a total `Ty`, so no call site changes shape. **The gap this leaves is closed by a conservation check at the end of the compile, and it is E184's R7 in another compiler.** A producer that has no token yet registers a promise: RUSTTYSTY:528 "    /// Constructs a \`TyKind::Error\` type and registers a \`span_delayed_bug\` to ensure it gets used." with the message RUSTTYSTY:531 "        Ty::new_error_with_message(tcx, DUMMY_SP, \"TyKind::Error constructed but no error reported\")", built by RUSTDCX:1078 "    pub fn span_delayed_bug(". At the end, an unredeemed promise is an internal compiler error: RUSTDCX:1479 "        let note1 = \"no errors encountered even though delayed bugs were created\";" RUSTDCX:1480 "        let note2 = \"those delayed bugs will now be shown as internal compiler errors\";", suppressed only when a real error did occur, RUSTDCX:1457 "            // If an error happened already. We shouldn't expose delayed bugs." **A refusal with no report is caught by a fold at the end of the compile, which is exactly what R7's `conserve` does over `FateRec`.**

  **7. THE THREE POSITIONS, AND WHERE EACH ONE PUTS THE OBLIGATION WHEN THE LANGUAGE GROWS A FORM.** **(a) Retype the producer.** The obligation is a compile error at the producer's `case`, which is where this tree's instrument lives (`lib/typing/kernel.chiral:1319`, `all-covered?` raising `(r-judged (subj-none) (jg-nonexhaustive))`, and it applies to a `case` with no default). Price is the count in item 1. Occupant: GHC's `TcRnMessage`. **(b) Re-walk on the refusal path.** The obligation is nowhere, and the drift is measured in item 2. Occupant: CPython, one, and it repairs the drift at runtime. **(c) The producer leaves a value the classifier reads.** The obligation splits by what the value carries. Carrying the full provenance (GHC's `CtOrigin`) puts the obligation back at the producer with the classifier's fall-throughs as the residue. Carrying one bit (rustc's `ErrorGuaranteed`) removes the obligation from both and replaces it with a whole-compile conservation check. **No surveyed system leaves a re-walking classifier as the sole account of a refusal.**
