### FD-41 the five headings surveyed are six libraries, GTK4 matches selectors and computes CSS 2.1 specificity while Halogen's selector-free path is selector-free by discarding, the four genuine ones declare exactly two objects in common, no third object is shared by even three of them, and eight objects the sources declare hold no roster row anywhere in this tree

- state:    OPEN
- claim:    The question: in systems that resolve style WITHOUT selectors and WITHOUT specificity, what is the minimal set of objects each one makes first-class and separately nameable, and what is the intersection across them. Posed so it can come back `no`, and part of it did. **Twenty-four pins added, every one origin `raw`. The answer: GTK4 CSS is not in the class at all, Halogen's is only in the class by discarding, and across the four systems that are in it the intersection is exactly TWO objects, a property identity that is a value distinct from the property's value and a scoping operator that binds it over a subtree; no third object is shared by even three of the four.** Two of the four do not declare the property identity themselves and borrow it from the host language, a Swift `WritableKeyPath` and a Dart `Type`. **Eight objects the sources declare as types or first-class values hold no row on any roster in this tree**, and the six rows in scope (`C3`, `C6`, `C7`, `C10`, `C11`, `C12`) name none of them.
- measured: **1. THE FIVE HEADINGS ARE SIX LIBRARIES, AND TWO OF THE SIX FAIL THE PREMISE IN TWO DIFFERENT WAYS.** **GTK4 CSS matches selectors against a tree and computes specificity.** The resolution model is stated in the overview: GTKCSSOV:121 "the selectors against a tree of nodes. Each node in the tree has a" name, a state and possibly style classes, and GTKCSSOV:145 "Selectors work very similar to the way they do on the&nbsp;web.". The arbiter is in the source and it is the web's: GTKCSSSEL:1730 "/* Computes specificity according to CSS 2.1." over a three-counter ids/classes/elements triple. **The deliberate subset is on the property vocabulary only.** Extracted from the pinned table by its own cell pattern, `GTKCSSPROP` lists 117 property names, of which 10 are `-gtk-` custom properties and 3 are media features; `display`, `position` and every flex property are absent, and so are `width`, `height`, `top` and `left`. The registry behind them is 94 longhand registrations in `GTKCSSIMPL`. **GTK4 is a property-vocabulary subset of web CSS with the web's resolution model intact, which is the opposite of what this survey was looking for, and it is the most useful single correction this run makes to the dispatch brief.** **Halogen reaches selector-freedom by discarding.** `purescript-css`, which the Halogen adapter is an adapter for, declares selectors outright: PSCSSSHEET:15 "import CSS.Selector (Selector, Refinement)", and its rule sum PSCSSSHEET:52 "data Rule" carries `Nested`, `Query`, `Face`, `Keyframe` and `Import` beside PSCSSSHEET:53 "  = Property (Key Unit) Value". The selector-free path is the inline-style renderer, and it is selector-free because it throws the rest away: HALOCSS:53 "  property ∷ Rule → Maybe (Tuple (Key Unit) Value)", HALOCSS:54 "  property (Property k v) = Just (Tuple k v)", HALOCSS:55 "  property _              = Nothing". Every nested rule, media query, font-face, keyframe and import silently vanishes on that path with no diagnostic.

  **2. ELM-UI IS GENUINELY SELECTOR-FREE AND IT REPLACES SPECIFICITY WITH TWO NAMED OBJECTS.** The attribute sum is ELMUIMODEL:302 "type Attribute aligned msg" with ten constructors, and two of them carry an identity beside the value: ELMUIMODEL:309 "    | StyleClass Flag Style", with the library's own word for what the `Flag` is at ELMUIMODEL:306 "      -- invalidation key and literal class". The resolution is a fold whose order is the argument list reversed, ELMUIMODEL:1560 "        |> List.reverse", and a constructor whose flag is already present is skipped, ELMUIMODEL:927 "                Class flag exactClassName ->" guarded by `Flag.present`. **So the conflict rule is last-in-the-list wins and the arbiter is a presence set, not a weight.** The two objects are declared in their own module: ELMUIFLAG:65 "    = Field Int Int", a 64-slot bitset in two 32-bit words, and ELMUIFLAG:121 "flag : Int -> Flag" which splits at index 31 into the second word. Its operations are ELMUIFLAG:89 "present : Flag -> Field -> Bool" and ELMUIFLAG:116 "merge : Field -> Field -> Field", and the module comments the whole apparatus ELMUIFLAG:133 "{- Used for Style invalidation -}". 47 flags are named. **elm-ui's property identity is an integer bit position and its value type is a separate sum**, ELMUIMODEL:290 "type Property" being the untyped string pair ELMUIMODEL:291 "    = Property String String" while the typed layer is `Style`, `Length` (ELMUIMODEL:341 "type Length") and `Color`.

  **3. SWIFTUI DECLARES SIX OBJECTS AND BORROWS THE SEVENTH.** The key is a protocol, SWIFTENVKEY:1 "A key for accessing values in the environment.", carrying its own default and an associated value type the compiler infers: SWIFTENVKEY:1 "private struct MyEnvironmentKey: EnvironmentKey {" then SWIFTENVKEY:1 "    static let defaultValue: String = " a literal, with SWIFTENVKEY:1 "The Swift compiler automatically infers the associated " `Value` type from it. The aggregate is a struct, SWIFTENVVALS:1 "A collection of environment values propagated through a view hierarchy.", holding 167 members in the pinned reference. **The identity used at the call site is not the key type, it is a standard-library key path**: the setter's signature carries SWIFTENVMOD:1 "s:s15WritableKeyPathC" over `EnvironmentValues`, and the modifier is SWIFTENVMOD:1 "Sets the environment value of the specified key path to the given value.". The reader is a property wrapper, SWIFTENVWRAP:1 "A property wrapper that reads a value from a view’s environment.". A macro generates the key type as a peer, SWIFTENTRY:1 "(peer, names: prefixed(__Key_)) ", and its abstract names four parallel namespaces that share the mechanism, SWIFTENTRY:1 "Creates an environment values, transaction, container values," or focused values entry. **The scope rule is the whole conflict rule**, SWIFTENVMOD:1 "as well as that view’s descendant views. It has no effect" outside the hierarchy it is called on. **What SwiftUI leaves implicit: there is no ordering object, no merge, no weight, no public snapshot type, no change predicate and no interpolation.** Lexical nesting is the only order and the innermost setter is the whole arbitration.

  **4. COMPOSE DECLARES THE MOST OF THE FOUR, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE THAT DECLARES ITS OWN KEY.** The key is a sealed class carrying a default factory, COMPLOCAL:59 "public sealed class CompositionLocal<T>(defaultFactory: () -> T) {", and its providable subclass COMPLOCAL:87 "public abstract class ProvidableCompositionLocal<T> internal constructor(defaultFactory: () -> T) :". Two constructors split the key by invalidation cost, COMPLOCAL:242 "public fun <T> compositionLocalOf(" against COMPLOCAL:272 "public fun <T> staticCompositionLocalOf(defaultFactory: () -> T): ProvidableCompositionLocal<T> =". **The binding is a separate object with five fields beyond the pair**: COMPPROVVAL:97 "public class ProvidedValue<T>" carries COMPPROVVAL:106 "    internal val mutationPolicy: SnapshotMutationPolicy<T>?," , COMPPROVVAL:108 "    internal val compute: (CompositionLocalAccessorScope.() -> T)?," and COMPPROVVAL:130 "    public var canOverride: Boolean = true", the last flipped by COMPPROVVAL:146 "    internal fun ifNotAlreadyProvided() = this.also { canOverride = false }" when the binder used COMPLOCAL:106 "    public infix fun providesDefault(value: T): ProvidedValue<T> =" instead of COMPLOCAL:97 "    public infix fun provides(value: T): ProvidedValue<T> = defaultProvidedValue(value)". **The aggregate is a declared public type**, COMPLOCALMAP:26 "public sealed interface CompositionLocalMap {" with one operation COMPLOCALMAP:41 "    public operator fun <T> get(key: CompositionLocal<T>): T" over a persistent map COMPLOCALMAP:54 "internal interface PersistentCompositionLocalMap :". **The snapshot is a second declared type**, COMPLOCAL:429 "public class CompositionLocalContext", and a computed binding reads other keys through COMPLOCAL:403 "public interface CompositionLocalAccessorScope {". The theme is one record behind one key, COMPM3THEME:108 "        _localMaterialTheme provides theme," read back through COMPM3THEME:122 "public object MaterialTheme {" as four fields. **What Compose leaves implicit: no ordering, no specificity, no per-property inherit flag, no interpolation.**

  **5. FLUTTER DECLARES THE FEWEST AND ITS KEY IS THE LANGUAGE'S TYPE.** The provider is a widget, FLUTRFW:1860 "abstract class InheritedWidget extends ProxyWidget {", with one abstract member and it is a predicate, FLUTRFW:1881 "  bool updateShouldNotify(covariant InheritedWidget oldWidget);". The lookup is keyed by the widget's own type and carries an optional sub-value selector, FLUTRFW:2465 "  T? dependOnInheritedWidgetOfExactType<T extends InheritedWidget>({Object? aspect});", resolved against an aggregate that is private and keyed by the language's runtime type, FLUTRFW:5060 "  PersistentHashMap<Type, InheritedElement>? _inheritedElements;". **The dependency is a first-class per-dependent record**, written at FLUTRFW:5094 "    ancestor.updateDependencies(this, aspect);" and read at FLUTRFW:6315 "  Object? getDependencies(Element dependent) {". **The snapshot is a declared type and it exists for an explicit reason**: FLUTRINHTH:36 "abstract class InheritedTheme extends InheritedWidget {" adds FLUTRINHTH:51 "  Widget wrap(BuildContext context, Widget child);" and FLUTRINHTH:133 "class CapturedThemes {" so that a subtree shown in a different context from the one it was built in keeps the environment it was built under. **There is no default on the key**: the reader supplies its own, FLUTRTHEME:122 "  static ThemeData of(BuildContext context) {" falling through FLUTRTHEME:133 "        inheritedTheme?.theme.data ??" to FLUTRTHEME:62 "  static final ThemeData _kFallbackTheme = ThemeData.fallback();". The notify predicate is value equality on the whole record, FLUTRTHEME:231 "  bool updateShouldNotify(_InheritedTheme old) => theme.data != old.theme.data;". The record is FLUTRTHDATA:220 "class ThemeData with Diagnosticable {" with 92 `final` fields, and **it declares an interpolation**, FLUTRTHDATA:1938 "  static ThemeData lerp(ThemeData a, ThemeData b, double t) {".

  **6. THE INTERSECTION, AND IT IS TWO OBJECTS.** Across the four systems that actually resolve without selectors and without specificity (SwiftUI, Compose, Flutter, elm-ui), exactly two objects are first-class and separately nameable in all four. **(i) A property identity that is a value distinct from the property's value.** SwiftUI: `EnvironmentKey` at declaration and a `WritableKeyPath` at the use site. Compose: `CompositionLocal<T>`, the instance being the identity. Flutter: the `InheritedWidget` subtype itself, used as a `Type` key. elm-ui: `Flag`, a bit position. **(ii) A scoping operator that binds an identity to a value over a subtree and nothing else.** SwiftUI `.environment(_:_:)`, Compose `CompositionLocalProvider`, Flutter the provider widget's position in the tree, elm-ui the attribute's position in the list. **Nothing else is shared by all four, and no third object is shared by even three of the four.** A default carried on the key: SwiftUI and Compose yes, Flutter and elm-ui no. An aggregate environment as a declared public type: SwiftUI and Compose yes, Flutter private, elm-ui absent (its `Field` aggregates which properties are decided, not their values). A reified transportable snapshot: Compose `CompositionLocalContext` and Flutter `CapturedThemes` yes, SwiftUI and elm-ui no. A change predicate: Flutter `updateShouldNotify` and Compose `SnapshotMutationPolicy` yes, SwiftUI and elm-ui no. An interpolation: Flutter only. A shadowing control: Compose `canOverride` only. A presence set: elm-ui only. **Two of the four do not declare their own key type at all and borrow it from the host language**, which is the second correction this run makes: a selector-free style system is not obliged to mint a key, only to have one, and the two that borrowed got the compiler's type-safety for free.

  **7. THE IMPLIED PRIMITIVES. EIGHT OBJECTS THE SOURCES DECLARE THAT NO ROSTER ROW IN THIS TREE NAMES.** Each is checked against `docs/arcs/` by grep and each returned nothing. **(a) The property identity as a value.** Implied by all four selector-free systems and declared outright by two, ELMUIFLAG:65 and COMPLOCAL:59. `C6` names an expression algebra over values, `C7` names an `Env` record, `C12` names shorthand constructors; `Attrs` at `lib/protocol/grid.chiral:12` is six `Bool` fields plus two `Color` fields, and a field name is not a value. **No row names a property identity, and `C3`'s "attachment by a pure function over the node" cannot be stated without one**, because the function's codomain has to say which properties it decided. **(b) The decided-set.** elm-ui's `Field` (ELMUIFLAG:65) and Compose's `canOverride` (COMPPROVVAL:130) are two shapes of the same object: what has already been resolved, carried alongside what it resolved to. `C2`'s fold is built and has nowhere to record it. No row names it. **(c) The change predicate as a declared object.** FLUTRFW:1881 and COMPPROVVAL:106. `C11` says the dependency is the argument list, which is the backward half and cannot express "the argument changed and the answer did not, so do not notify". No row names a predicate. **(d) The declared downstream-effect set.** GTKCSSTYPES:174 "} GtkCssAffects;" is 14 flags from GTKCSSTYPES:160 "  GTK_CSS_AFFECTS_CONTENT              = (1 << 0)," to GTKCSSTYPES:173 "  GTK_CSS_AFFECTS_TRANSFORM            = (1 << 13),", declared per property at registration, GTKCSSIMPL:67 "                                 GtkCssAffects                  affects,". This is invalidation stated forward, from the property to what it invalidates. `C11` names only the backward direction. No row names the forward one, and it is the one a compile-time system can check. **(e) The per-property metadata record.** GTKCSSIMPL:64 "gtk_css_style_property_register (const char *                   name," registers each of 94 longhands with a name, an id, an affects set, an animated flag, GTKCSSIMPL:79 "(flags & GTK_STYLE_PROPERTY_INHERIT) ? TRUE : FALSE," , GTKCSSIMPL:80 ", initial_value," and GTKCSSIMPL:68 "                                 GtkCssStylePropertyParseFunc   parse_value,". `C4` names the inherit sum on the value. **Nobody names inheritance as a per-property flag, nor the initial value as a property-level field, nor the parser as part of the property's own declaration**, and the three together are what makes GTK's table a table rather than 94 hand-written cases. **(f) The reified environment snapshot as a transportable value.** COMPLOCAL:429 and FLUTRINHTH:133, both declared, both for the same reason: a subtree rendered somewhere other than where it was built. `C7` names `Env` as a declared ADT and nothing names capture and re-application. **`C9`'s every-state gate needs exactly this**, because walking the `(Env, State)` product off-tree is rendering a subtree outside the place it was built. **(g) The interpolation.** FLUTRTHDATA:1938. Every animated or transitioned style value has to be interpolable, and GTK registers `animated` per property for the same reason (GTKCSSIMPL:64 registry). `Color` at `lib/protocol/grid.chiral:6` is a closed sum with no between. No row names a lerp, and `docs/arcs/` has one `lerp` hit and it is `E200`'s pixel compositing. **(h) The key-to-value type link, and the boundary where it is erased.** PSCSSPROP:41 "newtype Key a = Key Prefixed" carries the value type as a phantom parameter and PSCSSPROP:52 "cast (Key k) = Key k" erases it before the rule reaches the sheet, so the stored rule is PSCSSSHEET:53 "  = Property (Key Unit) Value" over PSCSSPROP:54 "newtype Value = Value Prefixed", a string pair. **This is a worked instance of exactly the defect `C6` is a restatement of**: the typing is real at the smart constructor and gone at the fold, in a library written in a dependently-flavoured functional language by people who wanted it typed. No row names the erasure boundary, and a gate on `C6` would have to test precisely that the link survives to the fold.

  **8. WHAT THE SOURCES DID NOT SETTLE, AND WHAT CAME BACK EMPTY.** **No surveyed system states a reason for the size of its object set.** Not one of the five carries a design note saying why it declares the objects it declares and leaves the rest implicit; the sets were read off the declarations. **No surveyed selector-free system publishes a conflict rule as a stated law.** SwiftUI's is a sentence in a modifier's discussion (SWIFTENVMOD:1), Compose's is the absence of one, Flutter's is tree position, elm-ui's is a fold direction in an internal module; none is asserted anywhere a test could redden. **SwiftUI is closed source and the four SwiftUI pins are Apple's own documentation JSON, not an implementation.** The `EnvironmentValues` storage, the merge on nesting and the invalidation are not observable from any pinned byte, so SwiftUI's "leaves implicit" list is a list of what Apple does not declare publicly and not a claim about what SwiftUI does not have. **Jetpack Compose's `LocalContentColor` and the rest of the material locals were not surveyed**; the theme reading here rests on `MaterialTheme.kt` alone. **Flutter's `InheritedModel` was not pinned**, so the `aspect` parameter enters this row through its two call sites in `framework.dart` and its own class is unread. **The Elm answer rests on one library.** `mdgriffith/elm-ui` is not Elm's styling, it is one package; `elm/html`'s `Html.Attributes.style` and `rtfeldman/elm-css` were not pinned, and elm-css is selector-carrying by construction. **GTK's media-feature set is three**, GTKCSSPROP:824 "Media queries can include" `not`, `and` and `or` over `prefers-color-scheme`, `prefers-contrast` and `prefers-reduced-motion`, and GTK declares no public type for them; whether that counts as an `Env` object is a judgement this row does not make. **No source in the survey ties any of this to a compile-time resolution claim**, so `C10` gains nothing measured from this run beyond the observation that three of the four systems resolve at run time and the fourth, elm-ui, resolves at render time.

## What an accessibility tree has to be derived from

### FD-42 no surveyed system derives an accessibility tree totally from an element model: all six derivations are total only because absence has a default, the one system that makes the role a required constructor argument is a push protocol with a second tree to keep in sync, the nine surveyed role sets run from zero to 182 and three of them are not closed, and ten objects the sources declare hold no roster row anywhere in this tree

- state:    OPEN
- claim:    The question: what must an element model carry for an accessibility tree to be derived from it by a TOTAL function, and which shipped systems derive that tree rather than maintain it as a parallel structure. Posed so it can come back `no`, and it did. **Twenty-one pins added, every one origin `raw`. The answer: no surveyed system derives totally in the sense `E3` means.** Six of the seven surveyed derivations ARE total, and every one of them is total for the same reason: **a missing role, name or state resolves to a declared default, so the element is never refused.** ARIA carries a thirteen-row fallback table at `SHOULD`; HTML-AAM mints a `minimum role` and otherwise `generic`; Flutter defaults `SemanticsRole.none` and `AttributedString('')`; Compose says not to set the role if yours is not listed; GTK4's interface default is `GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_NONE`; Android has no role at all and a null `CharSequence` class name. **The one surveyed system that makes the role a required constructor argument is AccessKit, `Node::new(role: Role)`, and it is the reference class `.planning/DISPLAY-LAYER-GAP.md` already names for `E3` — and it is a push protocol whose own documentation says the sender and receiver must be kept in sync, which is the definition of maintaining.** The derive/maintain split across the seven: the web and Flutter derive, Compose derives and then synthesizes nodes no element backs, GTK4 derives with a declared per-node escape to maintaining, Android and Apple maintain outright, AccessKit maintains by construction. **Nine surveyed role sets hold 0, 9, 20 (as a bitset, not a role), 60, 82, 85, 97, 131 and 182 members; no two agree, and three of them are open.** **Ten objects the sources declare hold no row on any roster in this tree**, checked by grep over `docs/arcs/`; the five rows in scope (`E1`, `E2`, `E3`, `E4`, `V1`) name none of them.
- measured: **1. THE WEB DERIVES, AND ITS OWN SPECIFICATIONS SAY THE DERIVATION IS PARTIAL AT EXACTLY THE PLACE `E1` AND `V1` AIM.** Core-AAM states the derivation as node creation, COREAAM:1133 "refer to the creation of" accessible object nodes within the accessibility tree, and there is no second author-maintained object anywhere in either mapping specification. **But the function is not total, and Core-AAM says so in the normative text.** For an element whose role has a required context and does not sit in it, COREAAM:1282 "the user agent behavior is not specified as a single rule", and the worked example is COREAAM:1290 "orphaned listitem. computedrole is unspecified". **ARIA then declines the validation outright.** ARIASPEC:13584 "user agents do not verify that an element wi"th a role of checkbox actually behaves like a checkbox, and in the same list ARIASPEC:13585 "Elements that do not correctly observe required child / parent role relationships or that appear elsewhere than in their required parent." **That is the web's two mapping specifications and its role specification all saying, in normative prose, that invalid nesting is neither refused nor resolved — which is the defect `display-calculus/E1` and `native-document/V1` propose to make unconstructible, and the single strongest external support either row has.** Where the derivation is total it is total by default: HTMLAAM:826 "expose an object using the mappings defined in CORE-AAM for the specified minimum role" for an element that would otherwise map to nothing, HTMLAAM:812 "role an element will map to if the element does not have a more specific implicit role or platform role mappings"; and for an element marked not mapped but forced visible, HTMLAAM:838 "\"Not mapped\" means the element does not need to be exposed via an" accessibility API while HTMLAAM:840 "map such elements to the role of" `generic`. An unrecognised role token is not an error either: ARIASPEC:13576 "treat the element as if no" role had been provided. **The mapping is a hand-written table, not a function of a type.** `HTMLAAM` carries 147 element mapping sections (3.5.2 to 3.5.148) over 110 distinct element-name strings; 26 of the 147 are qualified by context or attribute state, and `input` alone is 23 rows. Section 3.6 adds 162 attribute mapping sections. `COREAAM` carries 97 role mapping tables (3.4.3.1 to 3.4.3.97) and 100 state and property mapping tables (3.5.2.1 to 3.5.2.100), each role table mapping one role across five platform columns, MSAA+IAccessible2, UIA, ATK/AT-SPI, AX and Android.

  **2. THE ROLE SET IS NOT ONE SET, AND THREE OF THE NINE ARE NOT CLOSED.** ARIA 1.2 defines 94 roles of which 12 are abstract and forbidden in content, ARIASPEC:1503 "use abstract roles because they are not implemented in the" API binding, leaving **82 concrete**. `GtkAccessibleRole` is **85** C enumerators. AT-SPI declares **131** roles, `ATSPIACC:610` "- 130 - ATSPI_ROLE_SWITCH: A switch that can be toggled on/off. Since: 2.56" being the last, **and the set is explicitly open**: ATSPIACC:625 "    <method name=\"GetRoleName\">" exists because a role may fall outside the enumeration, ATSPIACC:619 "        Gets a UTF-8 string corresponding to the name of the role played by an object." AccessKit declares **182** in a Rust enum whose first member is a default, ACCESSKIT:63 "    #[default]" over `Unknown`. AppKit declares **60** role constants and **the set is open**: `NSACCROLE` is a `RawRepresentable` struct with NSACCROLE:1 "init(rawValue:)" among its members and NSACCROLE:1 "Values that describe types of objects that accessibility elements represent." as its abstract. UIKit has **no role at all**: UIACCTRAITS:1 "Constants that describe how an accessibility element behaves." is 20 constants conforming to UIACCTRAITS:1 "OptionSet", a combinable bitset whose members include `none`. Compose declares **nine**, CSEMPROP:853 "public value class Role private constructor(@Suppress(\"unused\") private val value: Int) {" — closed to outside construction by the private constructor, but a value class over `Int` is not exhaustively matchable, and the key's own documentation tells the author not to use it when it does not fit: CSEMPROP:209 "an exact role is not listed in [Role], this property should not be set and the framework will" automatically resolve it. **Android declares none.** `AccessibilityNodeInfo` has 79 public setters and its role carrier is a free string: ANDANI:3520 "     * Sets the class this node comes from." over ANDANI:3531 "    public void setClassName(CharSequence className) {", backed by ANDANI:1113 "    private CharSequence mClassName;" with no initialiser. Core-AAM's Android column confirms the shape from the spec side and also measures how much of the role survives: 103 `android.*` class cells across the 97 role tables, of which **66 are `android.view.View`**, the generic catch-all. **The three sets that are closed and exhaustively matchable are ARIA's 82, GTK4's 85 and AccessKit's 182, and they differ by a factor of 2.2. There is no canonical role set to import, and `E2` cannot name one without choosing.**

  **3. FLUTTER DERIVES, AND IT VALIDATES THE NESTING AFTERWARDS, IN DEBUG, WITH FIVE ARMS UNWRITTEN.** The semantics tree is compiled from the render tree with no parallel author object, and the annotation record is entirely optional: FLUTSEM:1667 "class SemanticsProperties extends DiagnosticableTree {" takes **77 parameters and not one is `required`**, while the flattened output `SemanticsData` takes **32 and every one is `required`**, FLUTSEM:1078 "    required this.role," among them. Totality is bought at the default: FLUTSEM:6034 "  SemanticsRole _role = SemanticsRole.none;" and FLUTSEM:6070 "  AttributedString _attributedLabel = AttributedString('');". **The structural check that `E1` says a closed per-context sum retires exists in Flutter, and it is a post-hoc tree walk.** FLUTSEM:162 "sealed class _DebugSemanticsRoleChecks {" switches on the node's role across 33 arms with no default clause — from which the `SemanticsRole` enum has exactly 33 members, since Dart 3 rejects a non-exhaustive enum switch, and the enum itself lives in `dart:ui` and was not pinned. Five of the 33 arms are unwritten, FLUTSEM:199 "      SemanticsRole.hotKey => _unimplemented," among them, and reaching one produces FLUTSEM:210 "      FlutterError('Missing checks for role" at run time. The checks that are written are required-owned-element checks in prose form: FLUTSEM:169 "      SemanticsRole.tabBar => _semanticsTabBar," resolves to a walk that raises FLUTSEM:291 "        error = FlutterError('Children of TabBar must have the tab role');". **The whole apparatus is stripped from release builds**: its one call site is FLUTSEM:4120 "      final FlutterError? error = _DebugSemanticsRoleChecks._checkSemanticsData(this);", inside an `assert`. Flutter also declares the two objects an element tree does not supply: a subtree boundary, FLUTSEM:5278 "  bool _isSemanticBoundary = false;", and a traversal order separate from tree order, FLUTSEM:7072 "abstract class SemanticsSortKey with Diagnosticable implements Comparable<SemanticsSortKey> {".

  **4. ANDROID MAINTAINS, AND THE CLASS DOCUMENTATION STATES IT AS A DESIGN PROPERTY.** ANDANI:82 "presented as a tree of accessibility node infos, which may or may not map one-to-one" to the view hierarchy, because ANDANI:84 " * a tree of accessibility node info." is what a custom view is free to report itself as. **The accessibility tree is explicitly not a function of the view tree, and the platform names that as freedom rather than as a defect.** Every carrier is a nullable field on a separately populated object: ANDANI:2413 "    public void setBoundsInScreen(Rect bounds) {", ANDANI:1113 for the class name, and a content description with the same null default. There is no role, no closed state set, and no required field.

  **5. COMPOSE DERIVES FROM THE LAYOUT TREE AND THEN INVENTS NODES.** The semantics of a node come from the modifier chain, CSEMMOD:68 "internal class EmptySemanticsModifier : Modifier.Node(), SemanticsModifierNode {" being the identity case, and the vocabulary is 64 `SemanticsPropertyKey`s in `SemanticsProperties` plus 36 in `SemanticsActions`. Two of those keys are the subtree operators, CSEMMOD:57 "    override val shouldClearDescendantSemantics: Boolean" and its merge counterpart. **But the tree handed to the accessibility layer is not the layout tree.** CSEMNODE:93 "    // We emit fake nodes for several cases. One is to prevent the content description clobbering" issue, and CSEMNODE:478 "    private fun emitFakeNodes(unmergedChildren: MutableList<SemanticsNode>) {" synthesizes children that no composable produced, built over CSEMNODE:525 "                    LayoutNode(" with `isVirtual = true` and identities carved out of the integer space by CSEMNODE:560 "internal const val RoleFakeNodeIdOffset = 1_000_000_000". **A derivation that adds nodes the source tree does not contain is not a function of that tree, and Compose's own comment calls the two reasons a clobbering issue and a temporary workaround.** Below this, Compose lowers into Android's maintained `AccessibilityNodeInfo`, so the end-to-end path is derive-then-maintain.

  **6. APPLE MAINTAINS, MOST EXPLICITLY OF THE SEVEN, AND THE TREE EDGES THEMSELVES ARE AUTHOR-SET STATE.** NSACCPROTO:1 "The complete list of properties and methods for accessible elements." is **294 members across 32 topic sections**, and they are getter/setter pairs throughout, NSACCPROTO:1 "Sets the accessibility element" being the opening of most of them. The section NSACCPROTO:1 "\"title\":\"Assigning roles\"" holds ten members. **The parent and the children are settable**: NSACCPROTO:1 "setAccessibilityParent" sits beside `setAccessibilityChildren`, `setAccessibilityChildrenInNavigationOrder` and `setAccessibilityVisibleChildren`, so on AppKit the shape of the accessibility tree is a value the author writes, not a projection of anything. UIKit states the maintain contract in a single sentence: `UIAccessibilityElement` is UIACCELEM:1 "that should be accessible to users with disabilities, but that isn"'t accessible by default, and a view holding non-view items UIACCELEM:1 "creates an instance of" one per item that needs to be accessible. Its whole carrier set is six attributes — label, hint, value, frame, frame-in-container-space and traits — and none of them is a role. The older AppKit surface is deprecated in place, NSACC:1 "A legacy, informal protocol that Apple doesn"'t recommend for active use.

  **7. GTK4 DERIVES BY DEFAULT AND PUBLISHES THE ESCAPE HATCH IN THE SAME PARAGRAPH.** Every widget is itself a `GtkAccessible`; there is no peer object to keep in sync, and the interface's own documentation says GTKACCC:41 "Normally, this tree corresponds to the widget tree, but can be customized" by reimplementing `get_accessible_parent`, `get_first_accessible_child` and `get_next_accessible_sibling`. For an accessible that is not a widget, GTKACCC:51 "it is necessary to ensure the correct shape" of the a11y tree by calling `set_accessible_parent`. **So GTK4's tree is a function of the widget tree only where nobody overrode it, and the override is a documented, supported, per-node facility.** The carrier set is four closed enumerations and one construct-time field: 85 roles, 9 `GtkAccessibleState`, 20 `GtkAccessibleProperty`, 24 `GtkAccessibleRelation` and 3 `GtkAccessiblePlatformState`. The role is immutable, GTKACCC:32 "The role cannot be changed after instantiating a" `GtkAccessible`, and its interface default is the bottom element, GTKACCC:94 "                       GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_NONE," — which is not a role but a deletion, because GTKACCC:1413 "gtk_accessible_should_present (GtkAccessible *self)" returns false for `NONE` and for `PRESENTATION`, and changes on such a node are re-parented onto its accessible parent. **Bounds are not a field but a partial query**: GTKACCH:150 "  gboolean (* get_bounds) (GtkAccessible *self," returns the rectangle GTKACCH:143 "   * parent's coordinate space, if those values can be determined." — the boolean is the totality gap made explicit. Below GTK sits AT-SPI, a maintained D-Bus protocol: the core interface carries eight read-only properties including ATSPIACC:30 "    <property name=\"Name\" type=\"s\" access=\"read\"/>" and ATSPIACC:39 "    <property name=\"Description\" type=\"s\" access=\"read\"/>", both plain `s` with no null, so an absent name is an empty string. **The interface set is 21 files and membership is queried, not guaranteed**: ATSPIACC:844 "        Returns an array of accessible interface names supported by the current object." Geometry is one of the 21, ATSPICOMP:90 "    <method name=\"GetExtents\">", so an AT-SPI object that does not implement `Component` has no bounds at all.

  **8. ACCESSKIT IS THE ONLY SYSTEM THAT MAKES THE ROLE REQUIRED, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MAINTAINS BY CONSTRUCTION.** `.planning/DISPLAY-LAYER-GAP.md`'s Lane E names AccessKit as `E3`'s reference class, and the pin bears the brief out on the primitive and refutes it on the model. The primitive: ACCESSKIT:1107 "pub struct Node {" opens with ACCESSKIT:1108 "    role: Role," followed by ACCESSKIT:1109 "    actions: u32," and a flag word, and the only public constructor is ACCESSKIT:1828 "    pub fn new(role: Role) -> Self {". **That is `display-calculus/E2` as written, shipped, in Rust.** The model: ACCESSKIT:3193 "/// The sender and receiver must be in sync; the update is only meant" to bring the tree from a specific previous state into its next state, unchanged fields must be resent verbatim, and ACCESSKIT:3215 "/// It is an error for any node in this list to not be either the root" or a child of another node — an error raised at apply time, not a construction the type refuses. Bounds are optional even here: ACCESSKIT:2533 "    (Bounds, bounds, get_rect_property, Option<Rect>, set_bounds, set_rect_property, Rect, clear_bounds)," is one of 88 `PropertyId`s beside 18 flags. **So the one system in the survey that pays `E2`'s price gets no totality for it: the role is required and the tree is still a second structure whose synchronisation is the caller's obligation.**

  **9. TOTALITY IS UNIVERSAL AND IT IS BOUGHT AT THE SAME PRICE EVERY TIME.** ARIA's table is the clearest statement of the price: ARIASPEC:13626 "attribute for a given role is missing, user agents" SHOULD process it as if a listed fallback were provided, and the table is 13 rows over 10 roles — `aria-checked` false for `checkbox`, `menuitemcheckbox`, `menuitemradio`, `radio` and `switch`; `aria-level` 2 for `heading`; `aria-expanded` false and `aria-controls` no-mapping for `combobox`; the midpoint of the range for `slider`, `scrollbar` and focusable `separator`. **It is `SHOULD`, so even the defaulting is not required.** The name is the same story stated as an algorithm rather than a table: ACCNAME:1000 "role prohibits naming, return the empty string" initialises the accumulator to the empty string, and the hidden-node arm is ACCNAME:1015 "Return the empty string." — **a role that ARIA lists as name-required and an author who supplies no name produce a node with an empty name and no diagnostic anywhere in the pipeline.** ARIA names 82-role-wide obligations that nothing enforces: ARIASPEC:1532 "at least one instance of one required" owned element is expected for a role that declares them, and ARIASPEC:1540 "If a role has a required context, authors" MUST place the element inside it. Both are author MUSTs with no user-agent counterpart, which section 9.2 then confirms. **Against this, the exclusion rule is the one place the specifications are total and normative in the strong direction**: ARIASPEC:13441 "elements</a> are not exposed via the" accessibility API and MUST NOT be included, for `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, the `hidden` attribute and a leading `none`/`presentation` role; and ARIASPEC:13473 "If not excluded from or marked as hidden in the accessibility tree per the rules above in" Excluding Elements, user agents MUST provide an accessible object for elements meeting the inclusion criteria. **The accessibility tree is therefore never the element tree. It is the element tree minus an exclusion set, minus fourteen roles' presentational children, plus whatever the platform synthesizes.**

  **10. THE IMPLIED PRIMITIVES. TEN OBJECTS THE SOURCES DECLARE THAT NO ROSTER ROW IN THIS TREE NAMES.** The check is a grep over `docs/arcs/` for each, and the corpus is 545 roster rows across every arc file (`grep -h '^| \`' docs/arcs/*-arc.md | wc -l`). Only four of the 545 mention a role or accessibility at all: `display-calculus/E2`, `display-calculus/E3`, `vocabulary/M6` ("a role carried, and no style") and `presentability/D2` (a doc-role table). **(a) The presentation predicate.** A per-node decision that removes the node from the derived tree. Declared by every surveyed system: ARIASPEC:13441, GTKACCC:1413 `gtk_accessible_should_present`, Flutter's `SemanticsRole.none` and `hidden`, Compose's `shouldClearDescendantSemantics` (CSEMMOD:57). `grep -rniE 'should.?present|excluded from the (a11y|accessibility)|not exposed|hidden from' docs/arcs/` returns **0**. **`E3` cannot be stated without it**: "derived by a total function" is a claim about a function whose codomain is a filtered tree, and the filter has to be part of the declaration or the function is not the one being claimed total. **(b) The subtree-merge operator.** Flutter's FLUTSEM:5278 `_isSemanticBoundary` beside `mergeAllDescendantsIntoThisNode`, Compose's CSEMMOD:57 pair, ARIA's Presentational Children characteristic over 14 named roles. Three independent systems declare an operator that collapses a subtree into one node. `grep -rniE 'presentational|merge descendant|semantic boundary|collapse.*subtree' docs/arcs/` returns **0**. **(c) The action set carried on the node.** ACCESSKIT:1109 "    actions: u32," plus a second `child_actions` word; Compose's 36 `SemanticsActions` keys; Flutter's `actions` int in the 32 required fields; AT-SPI's `Action` interface; Android's activation setters. Five of seven declare it and the two that do not are the two specification documents. `grep -rniE '\baction set\b|invocable|activat(e|ion) action|\bactions\b' docs/arcs/` returns **1 hit and it is `terminal-arc.md:122`, the VT escape parser's `Action` sum**. **(d) The node identity, stable across updates and independent of tree position.** AccessKit's `NodeId`, GTK's `accessible-id` vfunc (`GtkAccessibleIface::get_accessible_id`, GTKACCH:155 region), AT-SPI's `AccessibleId` property, Compose's `semanticsId`, Flutter's `identifier` among the 32 required fields. Five of seven. `grep -rniE 'node id|stable id|node identity|accessible id' docs/arcs/` returns **0**. **(e) The traversal order as a value distinct from tree order.** FLUTSEM:7072 `SemanticsSortKey` with its `OrdinalSortKey` instance, Flutter's `traversalParentIdentifier` and `traversalChildIdentifier` among the 32 required fields, and Apple's `setAccessibilityChildrenInNavigationOrder` as a second children array beside the first. `grep -rniE 'traversal order|reading order|navigation order|sort key|tab order' docs/arcs/` returns **0**. **(f) The accessible name, and it is neither the role nor the text.** `ACCNAME` is an entire specification for one string; AT-SPI declares three (ATSPIACC:30 Name, ATSPIACC:39 Description, `HelpText`); AppKit declares four (title, label, help, value); Flutter declares label, value, hint and tooltip. Seven of seven carry it and no two agree on how many there are. `grep -rniE 'accessible name|accessible description|content description|alt text|text alternative' docs/arcs/` returns **0**. **`E2` names the role and `E4` names the document's text form; nothing in this tree names the name**, and `E4`'s "every document has a text form" is a serialization, where AT-SPI's `Text` is a character-offset interface into rendered text and one of 21 optional interfaces. **(g) The typed relation edge with a declared inverse.** AT-SPI declares 23 relation types, issued in reciprocal pairs — `LABEL_FOR`/`LABELLED_BY`, `CONTROLLER_FOR`/`CONTROLLED_BY` — and GTK declares 24 `GtkAccessibleRelation`; Core-AAM gives relations their own section. `grep -rniE 'labelled.?by|described.?by|flow.?to|\bowns\b' docs/arcs/` returns 150 lines and **every one is the arc-ownership idiom ("`J5` owns the fix") or a template cell; none is an edge between two UI nodes**. **(h) The per-role required-attribute set, and its fallback.** ARIASPEC:13626's 13-row table, ARIA 5.2.2's requirement that a required state carry a non-empty value, and ARIA 5.2.10's per-role implicit value. `grep -rniE 'required (state|attribute|owned)|required context' docs/arcs/` returns **0**. `E2` proposes to make the role required; nothing proposes to make the role's own required attributes required, and the ARIA table is the measured list of what that costs. **(i) The synthesized node with no element behind it.** Compose's CSEMNODE:478 `emitFakeNodes` over `LayoutNode(isVirtual = true)`, and HTML-AAM's HTMLAAM:826 minimum role, which exposes an accessible object for markup that asked for none. Two independent systems inject into the output tree, and this is precisely why neither derivation is a function of its element tree. `grep -rniE 'synthes|virtual node|fake node|injected node' docs/arcs/` returns **0**. **(j) The two nesting relations, and they are not inverses.** ARIA declares required-owned-elements and required-context-role as separate characteristics and states in a note on each that neither implies the other. `display-calculus/E1` and `native-document/V1` both say "closed sums per context", which is the required-context half; **a single per-context constructor set collapses two relations the source says are independent, and no roster row names the other one.** `grep -rniE 'required owned|required context|reciprocal|inverse relation' docs/arcs/` returns **0**.

  **11. WHAT THE SOURCES DID NOT SETTLE, AND WHAT CAME BACK EMPTY.** **Not one surveyed system states a reason for the size of its role set**, and not one publishes a claim, a proof or a test that its derivation is total; both properties were read off declarations and defaults. **Core-AAM carries zero occurrences of "bounds" or "extents"**, so the web's mapping specification does not say where an accessible object's geometry comes from at all; `ARIASPEC` has three occurrences and none is a carrier. **Flutter's `SemanticsRole` enum was not pinned** — it lives in `dart:ui` in the engine repository — so the count of 33 is inferred from an exhaustive Dart switch with no default clause and is the one number in this row that is not read directly off a pinned byte. **No SwiftUI accessibility surface was surveyed**, and the four Apple pins are DocC JSON for AppKit and UIKit protocol documentation, not implementation; what UIKit derives internally is not observable from any pinned byte, so Apple's "maintains" verdict is a statement about the published contract. **Android's `AccessibilityNodeProvider` and `ExploreByTouchHelper` were not pinned**, so the virtual-tree half of Android's story rests on `AccessibilityNodeInfo`'s class documentation alone. **Compose's `AndroidComposeViewAccessibilityDelegateCompat`, which is the actual lowering from `SemanticsNode` to `AccessibilityNodeInfo`, was not pinned**; the derive-then-maintain claim rests on the two ends and not on the seam. **GTK's `GtkATContext` and its AT-SPI backend were not pinned**, so "GTK's tree is the widget tree" rests on `gtkaccessible.c`'s own documentation comment and on `should_present`. **No browser engine was surveyed**: Chromium's and WebKit's `AXObject` implementations are unread, so "the web derives" is what the specifications require and not what an engine was measured doing. **Nothing in the survey ties any of this to a compile-time check.** Six of the seven systems resolve at run time; the seventh, AccessKit, resolves at serialization time. `E3`'s word "total" has no counterpart in any pinned source.

  **2. SVG DECLARES A CONTENT MODEL AND FORBIDS ITS READER FROM ENFORCING IT.** Every SVG element carries a `Content model:` clause naming exactly which elements may appear inside it, which is a declaration in the strong sense. The error rule then removes the reader's ability to act on it: SVG2CONF:735. SVG 1.1 required the opposite — SVG11IMPL:57 "        The document shall be rendered up to, but not including," the first element which has an error — **so the only surveyed format that ever required a reader to stop at a defect deleted that requirement in its next version.** SVG 2 goes further and mints an element whose whole purpose is to have no type: SVG2STRUCT:363 carries `id="elementdef-unknown">unknown</dfn>` with content model "Any elements or ch"aracter data, and SVG2STRUCT:369 "Unknown elements are all elements that are in the SVG namespace that are not" defined by this specification or any SVG module. Foreign namespaces get a third rule: SVG2STRUCT:2049 "must include the unknown foreign-namespaced elements in the DOM" and exclude them from rendering. **Honest limit: SVG 2's unknown-element rule is marked at risk in the pin itself** — SVG2STRUCT:366 "rendering of their child trees, and assigning the SVGUnknownElement interface to" unknown elements are both at risk, with no known implementations — so this is the published contract and not a measured browser.

  **3. FIGMA IS THE SURVEY'S ONE SHIPPED TAGGED SUM WITH A PER-CONTEXT RESTRICTION, AND IT CLOSES NOTHING ELSE.** `Node` is a `oneOf` over **28** node schemas with `discriminator: propertyName: type` and a 28-entry mapping, FIGMAAPI:3988 "    Node:" and FIGMAAPI:4047 "          DOCUMENT: \"#/components/schemas/DocumentNode\"". `SubcanvasNode` is the same discriminator over **26** — the same constructors minus `DOCUMENT` and `CANVAS` — and `HasChildrenTrait` points a container's `children` at that 26-arm sum rather than at the 28-arm one. **That is `display-calculus/E1` and `vocabulary/F1`'s "closed sums per context", shipped, in a published schema, and it is the strongest external support either row has.** Against it: the sum is closed on the tag and open on everything else. `additionalProperties: false` occurs **zero times** in 372 schemas and 27 `*Trait` mixins; each node's own arm requires only its `type`, with the rest arriving through traits; and the field that would let a reader decide whether it understands the file, `schemaVersion`, is a bare `number` with `default: 0` and no documented meaning for any value. The `.fig` on-disk format is undocumented and **was not sourced**; this row is the REST document schema only.

  **4. GLTF AND EBML AGREE ON THE NUMBER ONE AND DISAGREE ON EVERYTHING ELSE.** glTF's entire mandatory surface is `asset`, and inside it `version`; a node requires nothing at all, and the schema's only structural clause is the `matrix` / TRS mutual exclusion at GLTFNODESCH:90. Absence is resolved by rule, never by refusal: GLTF2:1755 "When positions are not specified, client implementations **SHOULD** skip primitive's rendering unless its positions are provided by other means (e.g., by an extension)." — **a primitive with no vertex positions is skipped, not rejected** — and GLTF2:1759 "When normals are not specified, client implementations **MUST** calculate flat normals and the provided tangents (if present) **MUST** be ignored." The word "reject" and the word "fail" appear in no normative reader rule in the specification. EBML reaches the same number from the other direction: it ships a real schema language, and six of its seven mandatory header elements declare a default, so the reader's only hard obligation is `DocType`, which declares `length: >0` and no default. Even EBML's error clause is permissive: EBMLRFC:2406 "   by the EBML Reader and the data accepted as such, depending on how" strict the reader wants to be, and EBMLRFC:2436 "   *  Missing EBML Elements that are mandatory in a Master Element and" have no declared default value is a **may-discard**, not a must-refuse.

  **6. WHAT THE SURVEY SAYS ABOUT THE `.manifest` SCHEME ITSELF, REQUIREMENT BY REQUIREMENT.** Requirement 2 (tag leads) is Figma's discriminator and is the one requirement every declaring format in the survey also holds. Requirement 3 (named fields) is held by Figma, glTF and EBML and by no self-describing binary container: PNG's IHDR and Android's `ResChunk_header` are positional, and their field names live only in the specification. Requirement 4 (anything distinguishing two rows is a field) is held by **none** of the eight as a stated rule, and is contradicted in practice by PDF, whose resource dictionary distinguishes two `ExtGState` entries by a name the content stream supplies. Requirement 6 (the module coordinate) has **no analogue in any of the eight**: no surveyed format declares which layer of a system its file is truth for. Requirements 1 and 5 are type-system properties the eight do not have vocabulary for. **What the survey supplies that the six requirements do not name is the reader's half: not one of the six says what a reader does with a construct it does not recognise, and that is the question every one of the eight formats answers first.**

  **7. WHAT THIS BEARS ON, FOR THE FIVE ROWS IN SCOPE.** `canvas/G1` (`docs/arcs/canvas-arc.md:74`), a canvas is `(-> Env State Node)`: **in four of the eight formats a `Node` is not self-contained.** glTF's node names its mesh, camera and skin by integer index into top-level typed arrays; PDF's page reaches its fonts and images through a `Resources` dictionary that may live on an ancestor; Figma's node reaches components and styles through document-level maps. The document-level table the node resolves into has no place in `G1`'s signature unless it rides inside `Env`, and there is no `data Env` anywhere in `lib/` or `prog/`. `canvas/G4`, a document carries no computation as a closed `State` sum: **every one of the eight ships an untyped escape hatch** — glTF's `extras` (GLTFPROP:10, whose `$ref` imposes nothing), Figma's `pluginData` and `sharedPluginData`, PDF's private keys, PNG's private-chunk bit, SVG's foreign namespaces, USD's custom data — so "closed" is a property none of them claims. `canvas/G8`, one value many hosts: **SVG's answer to the same problem is 5 declared processing modes and 6 software conformance classes**, under which a static-mode viewer and a dynamic-interactive viewer both conform while drawing different things from one file; `G8` names no mechanism by which two hosts may legitimately differ, and the survey says every format that reached many hosts had to name one. `native-document/V4` (`docs/arcs/native-document-arc.md:46`), the render seam into the window, and `goals/display` condition 2, the seam: **no format in this survey declares a seam at all.** Eight formats, and the reader's output surface is unnamed in every one; the closest is SVG's conformance-class split and glTF's `extensionsUsed`, both of which describe the reader rather than the seam.

  **8. WHERE THE AUTHOR'S DIRECTIVE ALREADY HAS ROWS, ON AN ARC NONE OF THE FIVE CITES.** `records/author-calls.md` section `## Added by the display review, 2026-09-22` directs that condition 2 owe a declared canvas file format in the `.manifest` line. **Five of the six objects that asks for are already rostered** — on `docs/arcs/vocabulary-arc.md`, not on canvas: `vocabulary/M1` "the mark has a file kind and the loader checks it" (`:70`), `M4` "an unknown mark is refused" (`:73`), `M5` "the version field, and a total handler over it" (`:74`), `F1` "closed element sums per context … Absorbs `display-calculus/E1`" (`:76`), `F2` "the size bound in the type" (`:77`), `F3` "node addressing. **the shard is built.**" (`:78`). **What is missing is not a design, it is a binding**: no row on `canvas-arc.md` or `native-document-arc.md` cites any of the six, and no row anywhere states that a canvas file is a `vocabulary` mark. This run makes no edit and names it here. **And the survey tests `vocabulary` requirement 3 directly** (`docs/arcs/vocabulary-arc.md:57-59`, "An unknown mark is refused and an unhandled version is named … forward compatibility is a version field the reader totals over, so degradation is never silent"): **five of the eight formats carry a version field, and every one of the five also carries an ignore-the-unknown rule.** glTF has `asset.version` and GLTF2:3085's must-ignore; EBML has `DocTypeReadVersion` and EBMLRFC:2419's skip; PDF has the closed header set and the ignored dictionary key; Figma has `schemaVersion` (FIGMAAPI:9271 block, lines 9315-9318) and no closure at all; Android's compiled form has a skip length and no version. **No surveyed format substitutes a version field for the ignore rule.** `M4` plus `M5` is therefore a position the survey finds nobody holding, which is stronger than the requirement claims, and the price is the thing every one of the eight bought with the ignore rule.

  **9. THE IMPLIED PRIMITIVES. Figma has `pluginData` and `sharedPluginData`. PNG has the private-chunk bit. SVG has foreign namespaces (SVG2STRUCT:2049). PDF has private keys. USD has custom data. **Six of eight, and the two that lack one are the two with no extension story at all.** `grep -rniE 'extension slot|plugin data|private chunk|vendor extension|foreign namespace|customData|escape hatch' docs/arcs/` returns **0**. `canvas/G4`'s "closed `State` sum" is a claim none of the eight makes about its own document. **(f) The document-level table a node reference resolves into.** PDF's resource dictionary (0 required entries of 8, PDFSPEC:5397), glTF's top-level typed arrays reached by integer index, Figma's `components` / `componentSets` / `styles` maps. `grep -rniE 'resource dictionary|resource table|shared definition|definition table|document.level table' docs/arcs/` returns **0**. **A `Node` in three of the four declaring formats is meaningless without it**, and `canvas/G1`'s `(-> Env State Node)` has nowhere to put it. **(g) The conformance class: a declaration of which subset of the format a reader implements.** SVG 2 defines 5 processing modes and 6 software conformance classes; PNG clauses 12, 13 and 14 define encoder, decoder and editor conformance separately; glTF hands it to an adopter program. `grep -rniE 'conformance class|processing mode|reader profile|declared subset' docs/arcs/` returns **0**. **`canvas/G8`'s "one value, many hosts" is the problem this object exists to solve**, and `G8` names no mechanism by which two conforming hosts may legitimately draw different things. **(h) The editor's carry-forward rule.** PNG3:2302 "          <td>Safe-to-copy bit: fourth byte</td>" is a per-chunk declaration, in the same four bytes as the ancillary bit, of whether a program that rewrote the file may keep a chunk it did not understand.
